So I'm very pleased to welcome today Gary Taubes, who is a contributing correspondent for the Percents magazine. His work has appeared in the New York Times, the Planting, the Esquire.

cues.en: Work has also been included in the best of the best American science writing and also has received three signs in the Society of Journalism Award from the National Association of Science Writers. He's the author also of Good Calories, Bad Carrots that I'm sure many of you know about and currently he's Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Investigator in Health

cues.en: policy research at the University of at Berkeley. So with this, we'll have Geertau talk about his latest book. Thank you very much. This book is basically, Good Calories, Bad Calories took me about five years to write and was 500 pages long.
cues.zh: 那么现在，就请 Gary Taubes 来聊聊他的新书。非常感谢大家。《Good Calories, Bad Calories》这本书花了我大约五年时间来写，足足有 500 页厚。

cues.en: This is a screen I used to use for this talk. And I had written that book hoping to get both the lay readers and to the public health authorities around the country and the medical research community, because the goal of these books are to convince people that, I mean, it's almost a cliche, but that our fundamental understanding of why we get fat of obesity is completely incorrect, and that a new paradigm is in order, and that...
cues.zh: 这是我过去做这场演讲时常用的屏幕。我写那本书是希望能触及普通读者，以及全国的公共卫生机构和医学研究界，因为这些书的目的在于让人们相信——虽然这听起来快成陈词滥调了——我们对于“人为什么会发胖”、对于肥胖的根本理解是完全错误的，我们需要一个全新的范式，而且……

cues.en: Google should change the foods that they're serving at their wonderful, healthy, low-fat cafes. So after Good Calories, Bad Calories came out, I wrote Why We Get Fat, in effect, to make it the kind of airplane reading version of Good Calories, Bad Calories for people who don't have the time. I got a lot of emails from people from doctors who asked me if I could write a book that their patients could read, from patients who asked me if I could write a book that their doctors would read.
cues.zh: Google 应该改变他们那些又好又健康、主打低脂的咖啡厅里供应的食物。所以在《Good Calories, Bad Calories》出版后，我写了《Why We Get Fat》，实际上是想为那些没有时间的人制作一个简明易读的“旅途读物”版本。我收到了很多邮件，有医生问我能不能写一本他们的病人能读懂的书，也有病人问我能不能写一本他们的医生愿意读的书。

cues.en: So in this lecture, why we get fat is actually based on the lecture. So once you see this, you don't actually have to read the book. Let me see if this works a little bit. That's better. This is just background. There's an obesity epidemic in the works. I'm not going to go over it because, as usual, I'm probably going to run a little long on this talk. The obesity epidemic goes along with the diabetes epidemic. Diabetes diagnoses have tripled in the past 30 years in the United States.
cues.zh: 所以今天的这场演讲，《Why We Get Fat》这本书其实就是基于这个演讲内容的。只要听了这个，你们其实就不必去读那本书了。我来看看这个好不好使。好了。这只是一些背景。目前正处于肥胖流行病的蔓延中。我就不细讲了，因为不出意外的话，我今天的演讲大概又会有点超时。肥胖流行病与糖尿病流行病是相伴而生的。在过去 30 年里，美国的糖尿病确诊人数翻了三倍。

cues.en: And let's see if this. Diabetes, obesity are associated with a host of chronic diseases that are known as metabolic diseases, which include fatty liver disease, atherosclerosis, hypertension, stroke, cancer, asthma, sleep apnea, osteoarthritis, neurodegeneration. Actually, Alzheimer's disease is a disease that's now associated with what's called insulin resistance and obesity.
cues.zh: 我们再来看看这个。糖尿病、肥胖与一系列被称为代谢疾病的慢性疾病密切相关，包括脂肪肝、动脉粥样硬化、高血压、中风、癌症、哮喘、睡眠呼吸暂停、骨关节炎和神经退行性疾病。事实上，阿尔茨海默病现在也是一种与所谓的胰岛素抵抗和肥胖相关的疾病。

cues.en: And one of the subtexts of the talk I'm going to give today is that the conventional wisdom is that as we get fatter, that increases the risk of all these diseases. And the fundamental problem is this getting fatter. And I'm going to suggest that the same foods, the same thing that makes us fat, also causes these diseases. So it's a sort of fundamentally different causality. So the question we want is, why do we get fat? Obvious question.
cues.zh: 今天我这场演讲的一个潜台词是，传统观点认为，我们越胖，所有这些疾病的风险就越高。而根本问题就在于变胖。我要提出的是，同样的食物、同样让我们变胖的东西，也导致了这些疾病。所以这是一种根本不同的因果关系。我们要问的问题是：我们为什么会变胖？这个显而易见的问题。

cues.en: And the official answers are obesity occurs when a person consumes more calories from food than he or she burns. Overweight is a result of caloric imbalance and is mediated by genetics and health. That's what the US Surgeon General, the NIH, tells us. So how many people in this room actually believe this and think it's meaningful?
cues.zh: 官方答案是：当一个人从食物中摄入的卡路里超过消耗的卡路里时，就会发生肥胖。超重是热量失衡的结果，并受遗传和健康状况影响。这就是美国卫生总监、NIH 告诉我们的。那么，这个房间里有多少人真的相信这一点，并认为它有意义？

cues.en: And it's not bad. I gave this talk at Tufts a couple weeks ago to the nutrition department. And the Tufts people have been behind every dietary guidelines for the past 20 years. And I asked how many people believe this. And literally nobody raised their hand. And then I said, are you kidding? Because if you don't, I can leave. And then everybody raised their hand. And then after the talk, they said, well, we don't really believe it.
cues.zh: 这还不错。几周前我在塔夫茨大学给营养系做了这个演讲。过去20年里，塔夫茨的人参与制定了每一项膳食指南。我问有多少人相信这个。真的没有一个人举手。然后我说，你们开玩笑吧？因为如果你们不信，我可以走了。然后所有人都举手了。演讲结束后，他们说，呃，我们其实并不真的相信。

cues.en: So here's a conventional wisdom. Energy in is greater than energy out, and that's why we get fat. We take in more energy than we consume. We overeat, you know, and the excess calories go to our fat tissue. You hear about this a lot of different ways that, you know, in the medical literature, they'll refer to over-nutrition. Positive energy balance is another way to phrase it. And often virtually every article you read on obesity, they'll say obesity is a disorder of energy balance.
cues.zh: 所以这就是一种传统观点：能量摄入大于能量消耗，这就是我们变胖的原因。我们摄入的能量超过消耗的能量。我们吃多了，你知道，多余的热量就进入脂肪组织。你会从很多不同说法中听到这个，比如在医学文献里，他们会称之为营养过剩。能量正平衡是另一种说法。而且通常你读到的几乎每一篇关于肥胖的文章都会说，肥胖是一种能量平衡紊乱。

cues.en: And when they say that, what they mean is we take in more calories than we consume, and that's why we get fat. So here's the general image of what's going on here. And what you want to do when we talk about this, one of the key things you want to do in any science is explain the observations. So we have this observation of an obesity epidemic, and we want to explain it by our hypothesis, which is that we take in more calories than we expend. And the way that's been done over the years is that
cues.zh: 当他们这么说时，意思是：我们摄入的卡路里多于消耗的卡路里，这就是我们变胖的原因。所以这就是这里发生情况的一般图景。当我们谈论这个时，你想做的一件事——在任何科学中你想做的一件关键事情——就是解释观察结果。所以我们观察到肥胖流行，我们想用我们的假说来解释它，也就是：我们摄入的卡路里多于消耗的卡路里。而这些年来一直采用的方式是——

cues.en: The idea is increased prosperity. This is what Marian Nessel, a New York University nutritionist wrote in Science. As we get richer, more food becomes available. We have less reason to become physically active. That food's on every street corner. You don't have to work to get it. And so we get fatter and fatter. Kelly Brown, now a Yale University psychologist, coined the term a toxic environment, which is an environment that promotes overeating and sedentary behavior.
cues.zh: 这种观点认为是日益繁荣。这是纽约大学营养学家 Marian Nessel 在《Science》上写的。随着我们变得更富有，更多食物变得可得。我们越来越没有理由进行身体活动。食物就在每个街角。你不需要费力就能得到它。于是我们越来越胖。现为耶鲁大学心理学家的 Kelly Brown 创造了“有毒环境”这个词，指的是一个助长暴食和久坐行为的环境。

cues.en: so physical activity. And as Kelly put it, he said, you know, cheese curls and french fries.
cues.zh: 还有体力活动。就像 Kelly 所说的，比如芝士条和薯条。

cues.en: Fast food joins for as much part of our environment as trees and clouds. Mothers keep their kids home from school. We sit in front of computer screens all day long and video games and television. So a lot of reasons to eat too much, not enough reason to burn it off. And the question we want to know, here's the hypothesis. Increased prosperity leads to overeating. Energy in is greater than energy out. And that leads to obesity and the obesity epidemic.
cues.zh: 快餐店就像树木和白云一样，成了我们生活环境的一部分。母亲们不让孩子去学校。我们整天坐在电脑屏幕前，玩电子游戏，看电视。所以吃得太多的理由充分，消耗掉的动力却不足。我们想探究的问题、也是这个假说是：越富裕导致吃得越多。摄入能量大于消耗能量。进而导致了肥胖，引发了肥胖流行病。

cues.en: And what we want to know is, is this true? Because this is a science, and in science, this is a hypothesis. So you just ask the question, is it true? Does it explain the observations? When I'm lecturing to nutrition departments and obesity research departments, I often want to piss them off in the beginning. It's part of my nature. And I'll say, let's pretend this is a science for a second and see if...
cues.zh: 我们想知道的是，这真的是事实吗？因为这是门科学，在科学里，这只是个假说。所以你只需发问：这是真的吗？它能解释那些观察结果吗？我去营养学系和肥胖研究部门讲座时，开头总想激怒他们一下，这是我的性格使然。我会说：咱们先假装这是门科学，来看看……

cues.en: This can actually explain the observations. And there are a lot of observations out there, but they're less than obvious. Right now we know we've got McDonald's on every street corner. We know a lot of people watch television. And we know a lot of people are getting heavier. So we put them all together, these associations, and we say that's the cause. But we could find populations that didn't have all these
cues.zh: 它是否真能解释那些观察结果。外界有很多观察现象，但并没有那么显而易见。现在我们知道街角到处都是 McDonald's，知道很多人看电视，也知道很多人越来越胖。于是我们把这些关联捏合在一起，声称这就是原因。但我们完全可以找到一些并未身处这般

cues.en: this toxic environment as we define it, and we could look to see if the obesity existed there, and one of the underlying contexts here, and one of my underlying hypotheses, also of any science underlying principles is Occam's razor. So we should find the simplest possible hypothesis. So we're going to work from the hypothesis, so whatever makes any population fat is what makes our population fat, until we have to change it. So here we have a photo. This young woman, or middle-aged woman, was
cues.zh: 我们所谓“有害环境”的人群，去观察他们当中是否存在肥胖；而这背后的背景之一，也是我的基本假设之一，更是所有科学的基本原则之一，就是奥卡姆剃刀法则。我们应该寻找最简短的假说。因此我们先假设：无论是什么让其他人发胖，那也是让我们发胖的原因，除非后续不得不修正。这里有张照片。这位年轻或中年女性，

cues.en: known as Fat Louisa. This photo was taken in 1902. And Fat Louisa was a Pima Indian. The Pima lived on the Gila River Reservation. Well, now it's the Gila River Reservation south of Phoenix, Arizona. What's little known about the Pima is today they are the poster children for obesity and diabetes in the United States because they have conceivably the highest risk of any population.
cues.zh: 人称“肥胖的 Louisa”。这张照片摄于1902年。Louisa 是皮马印第安人。皮马人住在希拉河保留区。也就是如今亚利桑那州凤凰城以南的希拉河保留区。关于皮马人鲜为人知的是，如今他们成了全美肥胖和糖尿病的典型代表，因为他们面临的患病风险可以说高于任何族群。

cues.en: In the 17th, 18th, 19th century, they were the most affluent Native American tribe. They were hunters and gatherers. They hunted in the nearby mountains. They fished in the Gila River. They raised sheep, not sheep, cattle, pigs. They had warehouses full of food available in the 1840s. When the first US Army battalion moved to the Pima territory on the San Jose Trail,
cues.zh: 在17、18和19世纪，他们曾是最富裕的印第安部落。他们是狩猎采集者。在附近的山里打猎，在希拉河捕鱼。他们饲养牛、猪，不养羊。在1840年代，他们的仓库里堆满了存粮。当第一支美军营队沿 San Jose Trail 开进皮马领地时，

cues.en: They reported that the Pima had this incredible amount of food available. And they were all lean and sprightly. And by 1849, gold was discovered in California. And over the next 20 years, in 20,000 to 60,000, 49ers went west through the Pima territory. And the US government asked the Pima to feed them, which they did, and protect them from the hostile tribes farther west.
cues.zh: 他们报告称，皮马人拥有多得惊人的食物。而且他们个个精瘦、充满活力。到了1849年，加利福尼亚发现了黄金。在接下来的20年里，有两万到六万名淘金者穿过皮马领地西行。美国政府请求皮马人给他们提供口粮，皮马人照做了，并且还保护他们免受更西边敌对部落的袭击。

cues.en: And then by the 1870s, 1880s, Mexican Americans and Anglo-Americans started moving into the Pima territory. And they overhunted the nearby mountains. They diverted the Gila River water to irrigate their own fields. And the Pima went into what they called the years of famine, which lasted for 20 or 30 years. And by 1902, when Frank Russo, a Harvard anthropologist, came to live with the Pima and wrote the
cues.zh: 到19世纪70年代、80年代，墨西哥裔美国人和英裔美国人开始迁入皮马人的领地。他们在附近山里过度捕猎。他们引走希拉河的水来灌溉自己的田地。皮马人进入了他们所说的饥荒年代，持续了二三十年。到1902年，哈佛人类学家 Frank Russo 来和皮马人一起生活，并写下了

cues.en: the seminal text on the Pima Indians, they were living on a reservation, they were struggling as farmers to survive, and it was, it was Russell who took the photo of Fadluisa on the right, and he said, many old people in the tribe, unlike the sort of classical image of the strong, you know, buff Native American, many old people in the tribe were actually obese and overweight, and this was an observation that was seconded a few years later by Alex Fredlica.
cues.zh: 那部关于皮马印第安人的开创性著作。当时他们住在保留地，作为农民艰难求生。右边 Fadluisa 的照片正是 Russell 拍的。他说，部落里很多老人不像那种经典形象里强壮、你知道、肌肉发达的印第安人，很多老人其实肥胖、超重。几年后 Alex Fredlica 也支持这一观察。

cues.en: who was the physician anthropologist who went on to become the curator of the Smithsonian Department of Physical Anthropology. So the point about the Pima was that they went from being affluent in the 1840s, that drawing was actually made in 1851, to poor in 1902, and they went through 30 years of famine in the middle. And 30 years of famine, you could think of as 30 years of being on a diet. And they should have been leaner, right? Because our hypothesis says,
cues.zh: 他是一名医生兼人类学家，后来成为史密森尼学会体质人类学部的馆长。所以皮马人的关键在于：他们从1840年代的富裕——那幅画其实作于1851年——变成了1902年的贫困，中间经历了30年饥荒。30年饥荒，可以看作30年在节食。他们本该更瘦，对吧？因为我们的假说认为，

cues.en: Poverty leading to prosperity causes obesity, not prosperity leading to poverty. And yet in the early 19th century, we have a high level of obesity observed by two separate anthropologists living with the tribe. If this was the only example, we could probably toss it and assume something else was going on. But there are a lot of examples of obesity in
cues.zh: 由贫转富导致肥胖，而不是由富转贫。然而在19世纪初，两位与部落共同生活的独立人类学家观察到了高肥胖率。如果这是唯一例子，我们大概可以把它扔掉，假设另有原因。但有很多肥胖案例出现在

cues.en: what we would call non-toxic environments. And one of the things that sort of pissed me off doing my research for good calories, bad calories, which took five years, is you only had to go to look for them to find them. And yet the obesity research community hadn't bothered, because they had settled on their hypothesis. It's all about overeating. It's all about taking too many calories. It's all about fast food joints. And so they never looked. If you go look, you'll find a lot of different populations.
cues.zh: 我们所谓的无毒环境中。我为《Good Calories, Bad Calories》做了五年研究，其中让我有点恼火的一点是：你只要去找，就能找到它们。然而肥胖研究界根本没费心，因为他们已经认定自己的假说。一切都怪吃太多。一切都怪摄入太多卡路里。一切都怪快餐店。所以他们从不查看。你去看，就会发现很多不同人群。

cues.en: Sue on the South Dakota Crow Creek Reservation in 1928. This was a study done by two University of Chicago economists. And this population was so poor that you could use it. You could put it in the dictionary next to the definition of dirt poor. They lived four to eight people per room. Something like 15 families with 32 children on the reservation were living only on bread and coffee.
cues.zh: 1928年，南达科他州 Crow Creek 保留地的苏族（Sioux）。这是两位芝加哥大学经济学家做的一项研究。这个人群穷到可以拿来当例子。都可以把它放进字典里“赤贫”的定义旁边。他们每间房住四到八人。保留地上大约15个家庭、32个孩子只靠面包和咖啡生活。

cues.en: There were no bathrooms. There was no plumbing. You had to get water from the river. And yet 40% of the women, 25% of the men, and 10% of the children were distinctly fat. And 20% of the women, 25% of the men, and 25% of the children were distinctly thin. And there were definite signs of malnutrition on the, you know, these economists documented all kinds of deficiency diseases among these.
cues.zh: 那里没有浴室，没有自来水管，用水得去河里挑。然而，40%的女性、25%的男性和10%的儿童明显偏胖。同时，20%的女性、25%的男性和25%的儿童又明显偏瘦。而且还有明显的营养不良迹象，这些经济学家记录了他们身上各种各样的缺乏症。

cues.en: these Native Americans. And this combination of obesity and malnutrition or undernutrition existing in the same population is an observation I'm going to come back to shortly. Many times, in fact. Okay, Africans, Americans, in Charleston, South Carolina, in 1959, 30% of the women are obese, 18% of the men. Family incomes are $9 to $53 a week. That's less than $400 a week in 2011 dollars.
cues.zh: 这些美洲原住民。而在同一人群中同时存在肥胖与营养不良或营养匮乏，这个现象我稍后还会多次提到。事实上会提很多次。好的，1959年南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿的非裔美国人，30%的女性肥胖，男性为18%。家庭周收入在9到53美元之间，折算成2011年的美元，每周还不到400美元。

cues.en: Zulus in Durban, South Africa in 1960, 40% of the women are obese. Women in their 40s averaged 175 pounds. Today in the United States, the average weight for adult women is around 165 pounds. Trinidad, early 60s, Trinidad is having a malnutrition, a famine crisis. The US government sends a team of nutritionists down to help out, and they come back reporting that a third of women over 25 are obese.
cues.zh: 1960年南非德班的祖鲁人，40%的女性肥胖。40多岁女性的平均体重为175磅。而今天在美国，成年女性的平均体重约为165磅。60年代初的特立尼达，特立尼达正经历营养不良和饥荒危机。美国政府派了一支营养学家团队前去救援，他们回国后报告称，当地25岁以上的女性有三分之一处于肥胖状态。

cues.en: They report obesity is a potentially serious medical problem in women. The per capita daily, the next year, an MIT nutritionist goes down to Trinidad to figure out what's going on. She studies a diet of the obese women, compares it to the diets of the lean women in Trinidad, and concludes that the per capita daily diet was less than 2,000 calories a day, 21% fat. Fewer calories than were recommended at the time by the Food and Agriculture Organization for a healthy diet.
cues.zh: 他们报告称肥胖是当地女性潜在的严重医学问题。次年，一位MIT的营养学家前往特立尼达探究原因。她研究了肥胖女性的饮食，将其与特立尼达消瘦女性的饮食进行对比，得出的结论是：人均每日摄入热量不足2000卡路里，脂肪供能占21%。比当时联合国粮农组织推荐的健康饮食热量还要低。

cues.en: Bantu pensioners in South Africa in the mid-60s. These are the poorest of a disenfranchised population. 30% of the women are severely overweight, and the mean weight of women over 60 is 165 pounds. Rarotonga in the South Pacific. 40% of the women are obese. 25% are greatly obese, grossly obese. This is 1971. And then factory workers in Chile in 1974. 30% are obese. Nearly 50% of the women over 54 are...
cues.zh: 60年代中期的南非班图退休人员，他们是被剥夺权利的人群中最贫困的群体。30%的女性严重超重，60岁以上女性的平均体重为165磅。南太平洋的拉罗汤加岛，40%的女性肥胖，25%严重肥胖、极度肥胖。这是在1971年。然后是1974年智利的工厂工人，30%肥胖，54岁以上的女性有近50%……

cues.en: obese, 10% suffer under nourishment. Okay, so there's a combination, again, of obesity and malnutrition in the same population, and most are engaged in heavy labor. So, you know, these are factory workers. They probably don't belong to a gym. They probably don't have gyms.
cues.zh: 肥胖，10%营养不足。你看，同一人群中再次出现了肥胖与营养不良并存的现象，而且大多数人从事的是繁重的体力劳动。所以，他们是工厂工人，大概率不会办健身卡，70年代智利的工厂里……

cues.en: in their factory in Chile in the 70s. They're not working out regularly. They're not training for marathons. They're probably not doing triathlons. But they're engaged in heavy labor, heavy manual physical labor. So we could assume on a day-to-day basis they are more physically active than we are. And yet 30% are obese and nearly 50%, half of them over 54. And here's the last study I'll show you. This is Mexican Americans in Star County, Texas in 1981. 50% of the women in their 50s are obese.
cues.zh: 多半也没有健身房。他们没有定期去健身，不跑马拉松，大概率也不玩铁人三项。但他们从事着繁重的劳动，繁重的体力劳动。所以我们可以推断，他们的日常身体活动量肯定比我们大。然而还是有30%的人肥胖，54岁以上的人群中更是有近半数肥胖。这是我要展示的最后一项研究：1981年德克萨斯州斯塔尔县的墨西哥裔美国人，50多岁的女性中有50%处于肥胖状态。

cues.en: 40% of the men in their 40s and the living conditions, most inhabitants are employed in agricultural labor and are working in the oil field. So again, very physically active population, you know.
cues.zh: 40多岁的男性中有40%，再看生活条件，大多数居民从事农业劳动，也在油田工作。所以再说一次，这是体力活动非常多的人群，你知道。

cues.en: But high levels of obesity. And there was one restaurant in Starr County, Texas in 1981. Starr County is on the border of Mexico, about 200 miles due south of San Antonio. And that was a Mexican restaurant. So again, this definition, there's no increased prosperity for many of these populations. There's no prosperity at all. There's no toxic environment as we would define it today. But something's making them fat. And we want to know what.
cues.zh: 但肥胖率很高。1981年，德克萨斯州斯塔尔县有一家餐馆。斯塔尔县位于墨西哥边境，在圣安东尼奥正南约200英里处。那是一家墨西哥餐馆。所以再说一次，按这个定义，这些人群中的很多人并没有变得更富裕。根本谈不上富裕。也没有我们今天所定义的有毒环境。但有某种东西让他们变胖。我们想知道那是什么。

cues.en: Why would these populations fat? So we can figure out why these populations were fat. We can probably figure out why our populations are getting fatter. So here's how this question was phrased in 1973. Ralph Richards was a universe, he was a British trained diabetes specialist who went to Jamaica in the early 1960s.
cues.zh: 为什么这些人群会变胖？如果我们能弄清这些人群为什么变胖，也许就能弄清我们的人群为什么越来越胖。这个问题在1973年是这样表述的。Ralph Richards 是一位在英国受训的糖尿病专家，他在20世纪60年代初去了牙买加。

cues.en: founded a diabetes clinic at the University of the West Indies, and in the early 70s reported that a third of the women over 25 were obese, and that obesity reached what he called monstrous proportions in this age group. And he said, it's difficult to explain the high frequency of obesity seen in a relatively impecunious society such as exists in the West Indies.
cues.zh: 他在西印度群岛大学创办了一家糖尿病诊所，并在70年代初报告说，25岁以上的女性中有三分之一肥胖，而且肥胖在这一年龄组达到了他所说的“惊人比例”。他说，很难解释在像西印度群岛这样相对贫困的社会中，为什么肥胖如此高发。

cues.en: when compared to the standard of living enjoying the more developed countries. He's asking the same question I'm asking, and we all should be asking, if poor people are so fat, our theory says it's the rich ones who should be fat. Malnutrition and sub-nutrition are common disorders in the first two years of life in these areas and account for almost 25% of all admissions to pediatric wards in Jamaica. So by sub-nutrition, he means not enough food.
cues.zh: 与更发达国家所享有的生活水平相比。他问的正是我也在问、我们也都该问的问题：如果穷人这么胖，那按我们的理论，该胖的应该是富人才对。在这些地区，营养不良和营养不足是生命头两年常见的疾病，占牙买加儿科病房所有入院病例的近25%。他说的营养不足，就是食物不够。

cues.en: Subnutrition continues in early childhood to the early teens, so the children are stunted and show signs of emaciation, and then obesity begins to manifest itself in the female population and reaches enormous proportions from 30 onwards.
cues.zh: 营养不足会从幼儿期持续到青春期早期，所以孩子们发育迟缓，并出现消瘦迹象；然后肥胖开始在女性人群中显现，并从30岁起达到极大比例。

cues.en: So here's that question asked again, exactly the same observation, exactly the same question 30 years later, this time by Benjamin Caballero of Johns Hopkins. And now, within this paradigm of calories in, calories out, of overeating, okay, when Richards asked in 1973, he had an open mind. He didn't know what the answer was. But now Benjamin Caballero thinks he knows the answer, which is the answer we all think we know.
cues.zh: 所以，30年后，这个问题又被提了出来，完全相同的观察，完全相同的问题，这次是 Johns Hopkins 的 Benjamin Caballero 提出的。而现在，在“热量摄入、热量消耗”和“吃太多”的范式里，好吧，1973年 Richards 提问时，他心态开放。他并不知道答案。但现在 Benjamin Caballero 认为他知道答案，也就是我们所有人都以为自己知道的答案。

cues.en: And he says, a few years ago, this was in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2005, an article called obesity and malnutrition, a nutrition paradox. He says, a few years ago, I was visiting a primary care clinic in the slums of Sao Paulo, Brazil. The waiting room was full of mothers with thin, stunted young children exhibiting the typical signs of chronic undernutrition. Their appearance, sadly, would surprise few who visit poor urban areas in the developing world. What might come as a surprise is that many of the mothers holding those undernourished infants were themselves overweight.
cues.zh: 他说，几年前——这是2005年《New England Journal of Medicine》上的一篇文章，题为《肥胖与营养不良：一个营养悖论》。他说，几年前，我访问了巴西圣保罗贫民窟的一家初级保健诊所。候诊室里挤满了母亲，她们带着瘦小、发育迟缓的幼儿，这些孩子表现出慢性营养不足的典型迹象。可悲的是，对于去过发展中国家贫困城区的人来说，他们的样子并不会让人惊讶。可能让人惊讶的是，许多抱着这些营养不足婴儿的母亲，自己却超重。

cues.en: And then he says, the coexistence of underweight and overweight poses a challenge to public health programs. Since the aim of programs to reduce undernutrition, which is get people to eat more, make more food available, are obviously in conflict with those for obesity prevention, which is make less food available. So we have a problem. And I put this, poses a challenge to public health programs in italics.
cues.zh: 然后他说，体重过轻与超重并存对公共卫生项目构成了挑战。因为改善营养不良的项目旨在让人们多吃、提供更多食物，这显然与预防肥胖的项目——即减少食物供给——产生了冲突。所以我们遇到了问题。我特意把“对公共卫生项目构成了挑战”这句话用斜体标了出来。

cues.en: Because the coexistence of underweight and overweight poses a challenge to your paradigm, your belief system. If you believe that the mothers got fat because they took in more calories than they expended, they took in superfluous calories that they didn't need, and the children aren't getting enough food, right, then you believe that the mothers are willing to starve their children to death so that they can sneak outside and eat a Snickers bar, in effect. And I don't know how many are, you know, this is a young audience, how many mothers are there in this audience?
cues.zh: 因为体重过轻与超重并存，实际上是对你们的范式、你们的信仰体系提出了挑战。如果你认为母亲发胖是因为摄入热量大于消耗热量，摄入了并不需要的多余热量，而孩子们却吃不饱，对吧，那你其实就等同于相信：母亲宁愿饿死孩子，也要偷偷溜出去吃一块士力架。我不知道在座的——大家都很年轻——台下有多少位母亲？

cues.en: How many of you would do that? Let your children starve so you can get fat, as opposed to perhaps the other way around, right? So you've got two paradigms colliding. We've got our paradigm maternal behavior that says species don't survive unless the mothers make sacrifices for their children. And we have the paradigm of obesity that says these mothers are just happily guzzling excess calories while they're watching their kids starve to death.
cues.zh: 你们当中有谁会这么做？让孩子挨饿好让自己长胖，而不是反过来？所以这里出现了两种范式的碰撞。一种是对母性行为的认知范式：如果母亲不为孩子牺牲，物种就无法延续。另一种是对肥胖的认知范式：这些母亲眼睁睁看着孩子快要饿死，自己还在开开心心地狂吃超标的热量。

cues.en: This is an anomalous observation. I started my career writing about high energy physics, and high energy physics, you know, they've just built this large hadron collider at CERN that costs, I forget, how many billions of dollars, all designed to just create an observation that their theory can't explain so they can proceed onward. Here we've had this observation going back to 1928 at least, and nobody cares. And my point is you have to throw out one of the two paradigms.
cues.zh: 这是一个反常的观察结果。我的职业生涯始于撰写高能物理方面的文章，在高能物理界，比如 CERN 刚刚建成的这台大型强子对撞机，花费了我不记得多少亿美元，全都是为了制造出一个现有理论无法解释的观测结果，好让他们能继续探索。而在这里，我们至少从 1928 年起就有了这样的观测事实，却根本没人关心。我的观点是，这两个范式你必须抛弃一个。

cues.en: And I'm going to throw out the obesity paradigm because my mother, may she rest in peace, would have killed me if I threw out the maternal behavior paradigm. Let's look at some other inconvenient observations. Eating less doesn't work. Our hypothesis is that if we eat more, if we take in more calories than we expend, we will gain weight. So the idea is if you take in less calories than you will expend, you'll lose weight.
cues.zh: 我打算抛弃肥胖范式，因为要是我抛弃了母性行为范式，我那已故的母亲怕是饶不了我。我们再来看一些其他令人不适的观测事实。少吃根本没用。我们的假设是：如果我们吃得多，摄入热量大于消耗热量，体重就会增加。所以逻辑就是，只要摄入热量少于消耗热量，体重就会减轻。

cues.en: All you have to do is create what's called negative energy balance. So you go on a semi-restricted calorie diet. And there are a lot of meta-analyses over the years, systematic reviews, showing how poorly these work. The Cochrane Collaboration a few years ago when they looked at this, the Cochrane Collaboration is a collaboration created just to do unbiased.
cues.zh: 你所要做的就是制造所谓的“负能量平衡”。于是你开始采用部分限制热量的饮食法。多年来有大量的荟萃分析和系统评价，都在表明这种方法的效果有多差。几年前 Cochrane 协作网研究这个问题时——Cochrane 协作网是一个专门为了进行无偏见研究而建立的组织。

cues.en: reviews of the data, their assumption being every other review of the data is biased, so we have to create a methodology that doesn't allow bias then or into it. And as they put it back in, I think it was 2002, I can't see my notes, unfortunately, because we're not in notes mode here.
cues.zh: 对数据的综述，他们的假设是其他所有数据综述都有偏倚，所以我们必须建立一套不让偏倚进入的方法。正如他们所说，那大概是在2002年；可惜我看不到笔记，因为这里不是笔记模式。

cues.en: The weight loss achieved, that was 2002, is so small as to be clinically insignificant. And what you see in the literature is fascinating is because people are trying, they try to deal with this when they write about obesity, the fact that eating less doesn't work. But they believe that a calorie restricted diet is crucial. So you'll see these chapters in obesity textbooks, like the task force of obesity task force textbook, where the
cues.zh: 所实现的减重——那是在2002年——小到在临床上不显著。而你在文献中看到的东西很有意思，因为人们试图……他们在写肥胖问题时试图处理这一点，即少吃没用。但他们相信限制热量饮食至关重要。所以你会在肥胖教科书里看到这些章节，比如肥胖特别工作组的那本教科书，其中……

cues.en: Research will write that restricting calories is the fundamental approach. I forget the word they use because I don't have my notes. To curing obesity, and yet it rarely, if ever, works. Exercising more also doesn't work. And one of the problems here, I could also show you meta-analyses that talk about how clinically insignificant this effect is.
cues.zh: 研究者会写道，限制热量是根本方法。我忘了他们用的词，因为我没有笔记。用于治愈肥胖，但它很少有效，甚至几乎从未有效。多运动也没用。这里的问题之一是，我也可以给你们看一些荟萃分析，它们说明这种效应在临床上有多不显著。

cues.en: The best evidence I've found so far for this is American Heart Association, the American College of Sports Medicine in 2007, put out their physical activity guidelines, okay? And the physical activity guidelines, these are people, two organizations that want us to engage in healthy lifestyles that believe that physical activity should make a difference, and you would expect them to spin the data in favor of physical activity for exercise.
cues.zh: 到目前为止我找到的最好证据是，美国心脏协会和美国运动医学会在2007年发布了身体活动指南，对吧？而这些身体活动指南——这两个组织希望我们采取健康生活方式，也相信身体活动应该起作用，你本以为他们会把数据往有利于运动身体活动的方向解读。

cues.en: for weight loss. And the way they put it is this. They said it's reasonable to assume that persons with relatively high daily energy expenditures would be less likely to gain weight over time compared with those who have low energy expenditures. That's logically equivalent to saying it's reasonable to assume that if you're a couch potato and you increase your energy expenditure, you will be less likely to gain weight than if you remain a couch potato. And then they say so far data to support this hypothesis are not particularly compelling.
cues.zh: 用于减重。他们的说法是这样。他们说，有理由假设，与每日能量消耗较低的人相比，每日能量消耗相对较高的人随着时间推移更不容易增重。这在逻辑上等同于说，有理由假设，如果你是个沙发土豆，并且增加能量消耗，你就比继续当沙发土豆更不容易增重。然后他们说，到目前为止，支持这一假设的数据并不特别有说服力。

cues.en: And the point of this is this hypothesis is in the neighborhood of 100 to 150 years old. You could find obesity texts in the 1860s in which somebody like William Banting talks about his doctor telling him to go for a row every morning to burn off calories. He also talks about how it didn't help. You could find it by the 1890s when the laws of thermodynamics had been shown to hold.
cues.zh: 这个问题的要点是，这个假设大约有100到150年历史。你可以在19世纪60年代的肥胖论著中找到，像William Banting这样的人谈到他的医生叫他每天早上划船来燃烧卡路里。他还谈到这并没有帮助。到19世纪90年代你也能找到，当时热力学定律已被证明成立。

cues.en: with inanimate objects as well, with inanimate objects, with living beings as well, with inanimate objects. Researchers said, hey, maybe if we just get people to expend more energy, we'll gain weight. I mean, they'll lose weight. And over the course of 100 years, 150 years, this is the best we could say about it. You know, data to support this hypothesis are not particularly compelling. And that's a bad sign.
cues.zh: 对无生命物体如此，对无生命物体，对有生命体也如此，对无生命物体。研究人员说，嘿，也许只要我们让人消耗更多能量，我们就会增重。我是说，他们会减重。经过100年、150年，我们能说的最好的话就是这个。你知道，支持这一假设的数据并不特别有说服力。这是个坏迹象。

cues.en: When I was writing about high energy physics, it was an unwritten rule of high energy physics by Pief Panofsky, who's the founder of the Stanford Linear Accelerator Center here. And Pief said, if you throw money in an effect and it doesn't get bigger, it means it's not really there. And the corollary here is if you've been studying an effect for a century, and the best you could say about is data to support this hypothesis are not particularly compelling, there's a very good chance.
cues.zh: 当我还在报道高能物理时，这里斯坦福线性加速器中心的创始人 Pief Panofsky 曾提出过一条不成文的规则。Pief 说，如果你往某个效应上砸钱，它却没有任何起色，那就说明它根本不存在。由此推导出的结论是：如果你研究一个效应长达一个世纪，而你能给出的最好结论仅仅是“支持该假说的数据并不是特别有说服力”，那么很有可能——

cues.en: that your hypothesis is wrong, that increasing energy expenditure and physical activity will have no effect on how much you weigh or how much weight you gain. And one way to think about this, and to this I owe a British blogger, imagine that I'm having, I'm hosting a dinner party tonight and I've got, you know, the ten last finalists from Top Chef Cooking. And they're making this amazing feast. And I send you all invitations and I say,
cues.zh: 你的假说根本就是错的，增加能量消耗和体力活动对于你的体重或增重幅度根本没有任何影响。关于这一点，有种思考方式——这多亏了一位英国博主的启发——想象一下，如果我今晚要办一场晚宴，邀请了《Top Chef》上一季的十位决赛选手来掌勺。他们正在准备一顿极其丰盛的大餐。我给你们所有人都发了请帖，并说：

cues.en: I've got this feast. It's going to be a ton of the best tasting food you've ever eaten in your life. Come hungry. What would you do to make sure you came hungry? And here I'll take questions. Anyone want to answer? What would you do during the day? Skip snacks. Eat less. And take a long walk. Exercise more. You'd work out. So the exact same things that we prescribe overweight people to lose weight are the two things
cues.zh: “我准备了这场盛宴，这会是你这辈子吃过最美味、最丰盛的一餐，一定要饿着肚子来。”为了确保来的时候肚子足够饿，你会怎么做？这里我想问问大家，有人想回答吗？你白天会做什么？不吃零食。少吃点。多走动走动。多运动。你会去健身。所以，我们开给超重人群用来减肥的处方，恰恰就是——

cues.en: that you're going to do if you want to guarantee that you get hungry and eat more. And we're going to explain that in a while, but you can see already that there's something wrong here. Here's another problem with our energy balance idea. Practicing energy balance is impossible. This is a new phrase you hear. The past two or three years, the idea there are now industry programs developed in collaboration with the government to help you practice energy balance, to make sure you match...
cues.zh: 你想确保自己感到饥饿并吃得更多时会去做的两件事。我们稍后会解释这一点，但你已经能看出这里面有问题了。我们关于“能量平衡”的想法还存在另一个问题：践行能量平衡根本是不可能的。这是你过去两三年里能听到的一个新说法，现在甚至出现了与政府合作开发的企业项目，来帮助你践行能量平衡，确保你做到……

cues.en: calories into calories out so you don't gain weight. And the industry loves the idea, the food industry loves the idea of obesity being all about calories because you can't demonize anything. It's all about just it's your fault if you're overweight, you just have to eat less and exercise more. And if you want to build a gym in your neighborhood or a track or a park, go to Coke or Pepsi and ask them for money, they'll give it to you because they would like you to exercise more so that way they can't be blamed for your obesity epidemic.
cues.zh: 卡路里摄入与消耗平衡，这样你就不会长胖。食品行业非常喜欢“肥胖完全归咎于卡路里”这种说法，因为这样你就无法去妖魔化任何特定食物。这完全变成了“超重是你自己的错，你只需要少吃多运动就行了”。如果你想在社区建个健身房、跑道或公园，去找可口可乐或百事可乐要赞助，他们肯定会给钱，因为他们巴不得你多运动，这样肥胖流行的罪责就落不到他们头上了。

cues.en: So let's see what it takes to actually practice energy balance. A typical American's food intake is about 2,700 calories a day, okay? That's men and women. So that's a million calories a year, 10 million calories in a decade, okay? It's about 10 to 12 tons of food per decade. Now, all you'd have to do is ask the question. Let's say right now I'm a 25-year-old and I'm lean.
cues.zh: 那么，让我们来看看真正践行能量平衡需要做到什么程度。一个普通美国人一天的食物摄入量约为 2700 卡路里，对吧？这是把男女都算在内的平均值。也就是说一年一百万卡路里，十年一千万卡路里，对吧？这相当于每十年吃掉大约 10 到 12 吨食物。现在，你只需要问一个问题：假设我现在是一个 25 岁的精瘦小伙。

cues.en: And I want to ask the question, how well do I have to maintain energy balance? How well do I have to practice energy balance so that I don't gain 20 pounds in a decade, 40 pounds in 20 years, so by the time I'm in my mid-40s, I'm obese, okay? What does that entail? Because that's what the government's trying to get us to do. And the answer is you have to maintain your energy balance at 20 calories per day.
cues.zh: 我想问的是，我到底得把能量平衡维持得多好？我得把能量平衡做到多精确，才能避免十年胖20磅、二十年胖40磅，避免到了45岁左右就变成肥胖？这到底要求什么？因为政府想让我们做的正是这件事。答案是，你得把能量平衡维持在每天20卡路里以内。

cues.en: I mean, this is actually a trick answer, because if 20 calories per day goes into your fat tissue that you don't burn, you will gain 40 pounds in 20 years. Here's a calculation that's pretty simple, very simple. Even I could do this, and I don't work at Google. 20 calories times 365 days a year times 10 years divided by 3,500, which is a number of calories roughly in a pound of fat, and you end up with 21 pounds in a decade.
cues.zh: 我是说，这其实是个带坑的答案，因为如果每天有20卡路里进入脂肪组织却没被消耗，你二十年后就会胖40磅。这个计算很简单，非常简单。连我都能算，我又不在Google工作。20卡路里 × 一年365天 × 10年 ÷ 3500，3500大约是一磅脂肪所含的卡路里数，结果是十年胖21磅。

cues.en: Okay, so if you go over that if you can match your energy into your energy out to 20 calories a day and not exceed that on average You only gain 40 pounds if you only want to gain 20 pounds It's 10 calories if you don't want to gain any weight of course the idea is you have to do it perfectly 40 20 calories a day is 0.8 percent accuracy Nobody can do that nobody even I'm I will bet my life's income It's about that big that the world champion calorie counter
cues.zh: 好，所以如果你超出这个范围——如果你能把能量摄入和能量消耗匹配到每天20卡路里以内，并且平均不超标——你二十年也只会胖40磅；如果你只想胖20磅，那就是10卡路里；如果你一点体重都不想增加，那当然就得做到完美。可每天20卡路里意味着0.8%的准确度。没人能做到。没人，甚至我敢拿我一辈子的收入打赌，全世界最厉害的卡路里计算者——

cues.en: Guinness, if there is such an entry in Guinness, cannot gauge within 20 calories how much food they're eating per day. And then you have no idea how much you're expending. You're just guessing even when you go in to do research sessions. They just do calculations. So, you know, the point here is I got this calculation from a 1937 nutrition and metabolism textbook written by a fellow named Eugene Dubois who was a leading expert on metabolism in the United States pre-World War II. And Dubois used this calculation. He said, what's interesting about it,
cues.zh: Guinness，如果Guinness里真有这一项的话，也无法把每天吃进的食物的误差控制在20卡路里以内。而你根本不知道自己消耗了多少。你只能猜，哪怕去做研究测试时也一样。他们也只是做计算。所以重点是，我这个计算来自1937年的一本营养与代谢教科书，作者叫Eugene Dubois，他是二战前美国新陈代谢领域的顶尖专家。Dubois用过这个计算。他说，有趣的是，

cues.en: is, since nobody can do that, how do we maintain our weights? The question is, why are some of us fat? The question should be, why aren't all of us fat? Because if you overshoot by even 20 calories a day, on average, you're going to end up getting obese. And you can say, OK, maybe one way to do it is, I watch my weight, I look in the mirror, I see I'm getting fatter, my belt's getting snug, or my pants, or my...
cues.zh: 既然没人能做到，那我们又是怎么维持体重的？问题变成了：为什么我们当中有些人会胖？而问题其实应该是：为什么不是我们所有人都胖？因为如果你平均每天哪怕多摄入20卡路里，你最终都会变肥胖。你可能会说，好吧，也许有个办法是：我盯着自己的体重，照镜子，看到自己变胖了，腰带变紧了，或者裤子、或者我的……

cues.en: You know, a skirt doesn't fit, so therefore I'm going to eat less for a while until I get my weight back, so you oscillate around perfect energy balance. But then you have to ask the question, how do animals do it? Because they don't. They're not looking in the mirror. They don't have clothes they're putting on. So how do they maintain their weight? And virtually all animals do. They don't get chronically obese. So the idea that DuBois is obviously something else is going on here, other than consciously maturing calories into calories out, which none of us can do. So let's look at some other.
cues.zh: 你知道，裙子不合身了，所以接下来一段时间我少吃点，直到体重降回来，于是你就在完美能量平衡附近来回摆动。但接着你就得问：动物是怎么做到的？因为它们并不这么做。它们不照镜子。它们也不穿衣服。那它们怎么维持体重？而且几乎所有动物都能做到。它们不会长期肥胖。所以DuBois那个说法显然说明，这里还有别的机制在起作用，而不是我们有意识地把摄入卡路里和消耗卡路里匹配起来——这我们谁都做不到。所以让我们看看其他因素。

cues.en: Inconvenient observations. Genetics is one of them. I got to apologize now. If you go to an obesity textbook today, you will not see photos of naked human beings. But if you go to an obesity textbook pre-World War II, you would because those researchers, those clinicians thought you could learn a lot about watching how people fatten.
cues.zh: 令人困扰的观察结果，基因就是其中之一。我得先道个歉，如果你现在去看一本肥胖症教科书，是看不到人体裸照的。但要是看二战前的肥胖症教材，你就会看到，因为当年的研究人员和临床医生认为，观察人体发胖的过程能学到很多东西，

cues.en: as well as just whether they do or not. And one of the things I'm doing now is just channeling these pre-World War II researchers. And in fact, all I'm saying in my books is I'm taking the theory that German and Austrian researchers developed pre-World War II back when the Germans and Austrians did the best medical research in the world and there was virtually no meaningful medical research being done in the United States. And I'm taking that theory and I'm updating it.
cues.zh: 而不仅仅是看他们到底胖不胖。我现在做的事情之一，其实就是在重现二战前那些研究者的思想。事实上，我在书里所说的，无非是继承了德国和奥地利学者在二战前发展的理论，并对其进行更新；毕竟当年德奥两国的医学研究冠绝全球，而美国几乎没有任何有价值的医学研究。

cues.en: Okay, because they didn't survive the war, that community didn't survive the war. So for starters, here's genetics. Here's a pair of, and this comes from a 1940 textbook. Here's a pair of lean identical twins. Here's a pair of obese identical twins. Our overeating hypothesis might explain why these women are fatter than these women. These took in too many calories, and these practiced perfect energy balance. But what about this combination? Why do they have the same body type?
cues.zh: 因为那个学术圈子没能在战火中幸存下来。那么首先来看看基因。这是一对——出自1940年的一本教科书——这是一对消瘦的同卵双胞胎，这是一对肥胖的同卵双胞胎。暴饮暴食假说或许能解释为什么右边这些女性比左边更胖：右边摄入了过多热量，而左边维持了完美的能量平衡。但这种情况又怎么解释？为什么她们俩的身材一模一样？

cues.en: And why do they have the same body type? It's been known since the 1930s that obesity has a strong genetic component. Identical twins, it's not just their faces that look alike, their body types are the same too. So what's going on here? What do these genes determine? Do they determine exactly how much these women, how many forkfuls of food these women overate over 20, 30, 40 years, and exactly how long they sat on the couch versus going for a walk?
cues.zh: 为什么她们的身材也一模一样？早在20世纪30年代人们就知道，肥胖有很强的遗传因素。同卵双胞胎不仅长相相似，连体型也完全相同。那么这背后到底是怎么回事？这些基因究竟决定了什么？难道它们能精确决定这些女性在二三十甚至四十年里，每一口多吃了多少食物，以及她们坐在沙发上的时间与去散步的时间到底有多精确的比例吗？

cues.en: Or did they determine something else about how much and where they accumulated fat? Because they have the identical body. Here's a different variation of an animal husbandry. And it's even easier to see here what I'm talking about. You know, farmers, livestock breeders have been breeding more or less fatty cows, pigs, sheep for centuries probably. And here's a particularly fat breed of beef cattle. This is an Aberdeen Angus.
cues.zh: 还是说，基因决定了它们储存脂肪的数量和部位？因为她们的体型完全一致。我们在畜牧业中也能看到类似的变异，而且在这里更容易看清我想表达的意思。几个世纪以来，农夫和牲畜繁育者一直在培育体脂或多或少的牛、猪和羊。这里就有一种特别容易发胖的肉牛品种——阿伯丁安格斯牛（Aberdeen Angus）。

cues.en: Here's the meat. I should say it's stocky. It's very young. But you could see all the subcutaneous fat, the intramuscular fat here. And here's a lean species, a lean breed of cattle, a Jersey cow. And you could see the ribs showing. You could see the swollen otter. It's definitely a dairy cow. And you could ask yourself, simply, you know, they're different breeds. Obviously, different genes are determining how much they get fat. What exactly is going on here? What are these genes determining?
cues.zh: 这是肉质部分，应该说它很粗壮，还很年轻，但你能看到这儿所有的皮下脂肪和肌内脂肪。而这边是一个体型偏瘦的牛品种，娟姗牛（Jersey cow）。你可以看到露出的肋骨，看到肿胀的乳房，这显然是一头奶牛。你完全可以问问自己：它们是不同品种，显然不同的基因决定了它们发胖的程度，那这里到底发生了什么？这些基因究竟决定了什么？

cues.en: Do they determine how much these animals eat and exercise? Do they determine how many, you know, calories per graze or per bite of grass this cow takes? Or, you know, the Aberdeen Angus graze is for 12 hours, the Jersey only graze is for 10 a day. Does the Jersey, like, want to go to work out? So on the old Farsight cartoon, when it gets dark at night, the Jersey goes for jog, the Aberdeen Angus goes in and watches television, and it's obviously absurd.
cues.zh: 它们决定这些动物吃多少、运动多少吗？它们决定这头牛每轮吃草或每咬一口草摄入多少卡路里吗？或者，你知道，Aberdeen Angus 放牧 12 小时，Jersey 每天只放牧 10 小时。Jersey 是想去健身吗？在老的 Farsight 动画里，天黑了，Jersey 出去慢跑，Aberdeen Angus 进屋看电视，这显然很荒唐。

cues.en: Okay, whatever determines how much these animals get fat, we can be confident that how much they eat and exercise has nothing to do with it. More likely, you know, again, this is a beef cow. So what you want, it's effectively, brutally speaking, and I apologize for the vegetarians here, to the vegetarians here. It's a, you know, it's a machine.
cues.zh: 好吧，不管是什么决定这些动物长多胖，我们可以确定，它们吃多少、运动多少与此无关。更可能的是，你知道，再强调一下，这是肉牛。所以你想要的，实际上，说得残酷点，我向在场的素食者道歉。它是一台，你知道，一台机器。

cues.en: that takes in fuel here and deposits it here, and you want it all to go here. So you could assume that it just partitions the calories it eats into fat and protein. And the Jersey cow, you want to create milk, so you take in the fuel, and it's all going to go to the others to produce milk. And you don't want it wasting energy, in effect, bulking up. So maybe what these genes determine is not how many calories we take in, but how we...
cues.zh: 它在这里摄入燃料，在那里沉积，而你希望这一切都去这里。所以你可以假设，它只是把吃进去的卡路里分配到脂肪和蛋白质里。而 Jersey 牛，你想产奶，所以摄入燃料后，全都流向其他部位去产奶。你不想让它浪费能量，实际上，去长膘。所以也许这些基因决定的不是我们摄入多少卡路里，而是我们如何……

cues.en: partition the fuel we take in. That's a technical term. Sexual variations. Men and women fatten differently, okay? Men fatten above the waist, women fatten below the waist. Both these people would have had to overeat, taken more calories than they expend to get fat. This has doubled his risk of heart disease. This has not doubled her risk. If the weight's below the waist, it doesn't double your risk. What do the calories have to do with it?
cues.zh: 分配我们摄入的燃料。这是个技术术语。性别差异。男女长胖的方式不同，对吧？男人胖在腰以上，女人胖在腰以下。这两个人都得吃多，摄入的卡路里超过消耗，才会变胖。这让他患心脏病的风险翻倍。这没有让她的风险翻倍。如果体重在腰以下，就不会让你的风险翻倍。卡路里跟这有什么关系？

cues.en: And what do the calories have to do with where they get fat? Because obviously, that's a huge component of it. And another way to look at it is puberty. Men and women, when they go through puberty, boys, they begin puberty.
cues.zh: 卡路里跟胖在哪里又有什么关系？因为显然，这是其中很大的一部分。另一种看待方式是通过青春期。男人和女人，当他们经历青春期时，男孩，他们开始青春期。

cues.en: with roughly the same amount of body fat. When boys go through puberty, they lose fat and gain muscle. When girls go through puberty, they gain fat and breasts and hips and buttocks. And by the time they're out of puberty, the girls have about 50% more fat on their bodies than the men. Both boys and girls got bigger, so they both overate. They both took in more calories than they expend. But the boys lost fat and gained muscle. The girls gained fat.
cues.zh: 他们的体脂量大致相同。男孩经历青春期时，会减脂增肌。女孩经历青春期时，会增加脂肪，胸部、髋部和臀部也会发育。到青春期结束时，女孩体内的脂肪比男性多约 50%。男孩女孩都长大了，所以都吃多了。他们摄入的卡路里都超过消耗。但男孩减了脂、增了肌。女孩增了脂。

cues.en: in specific places. So you just ask the question, what did the calories have to do with it? What did the fact of their overeating have to do with whether or not they gained muscle or fat? And this is obviously controlled by sex and growth hormones, and that's an issue we'll get to. Now, lipidistrophes.
cues.zh: 在特定部位。所以你只需问：卡路里跟这有什么关系？他们吃多这件事，跟他们增肌还是增脂有什么关系？这显然受性激素和生长激素控制，这是我们后面会讲到的问题。现在，脂肪营养不良。

cues.en: This is, again, from the same 1940 textbook, which took it from a 1933 German textbook. This is a lipidistrophy called a progressive lipidistrophy. In the 1950s, there were about 200 of these on record. Most of them were in women. It's called progressive because these cases, they begin losing all subcutaneous fat in the face.
cues.zh: 这同样出自那本1940年的教科书，而它又是引自一本1933年的德文教科书。这是一种被称为进行性脂肪营养不良的病症。在1950年代，这类病例记录在案的大约有200起，其中大多数发生在女性身上。之所以称其为“进行性”，是因为这些病例中，患者的面部皮下脂肪开始全部流失，

cues.en: and their forehead, and it moves downward with time. One British physician recorded that his patient lost fat at about one inch a year. That's why it's progressive. And then it usually stops above the hips. And then they often get this lower body localized obesity below the waist. So the way these Europeans asked it, they said, are we going to blame the top half on under eating and the bottom half on over eating? Right?
cues.zh: 接着是额头，并随着时间推移向下蔓延。一位英国医生曾记录过，他的患者脂肪流失速度大约是每年一英寸，这就是为什么称它为进行性。流失通常会止于臀部以上，随后她们的腰部以下往往会出现这种下半身局部肥胖。所以当年欧洲学者的质疑方式是：难道我们要把上半身归咎于吃得太少，而把下半身归咎于吃得太多吗？对吧？

cues.en: And this is, again, obviously absurd. It's like a Gedanken experiment. But if this woman had 10 pounds more fat on her upper body, maybe even five pounds, just to smooth out her curves, her BMI was about 32 already just because of her lower body obesity. And she went into the doctor then. The doctor wouldn't recognize the lipodystrophy. And he would just say, look, eat less and exercise more. And the point that the Europeans are making is if you can't explain the localized conditions,
cues.zh: 而这显然又是荒谬的，就像一个思想实验。但如果这位女士的上半身能多长10磅脂肪，甚至只要5磅来抚平身体线条，仅凭她的下半身肥胖，她的BMI就已经达到了32左右。如果她那时去看医生，医生根本认不出这是脂肪营养不良，只会对她说：少吃点，多运动。欧洲学者想要表达的观点是，如果你无法用吃多吃少来解释这种局部状况，

cues.en: by under-eating and over-eating, why would you even think to explain the generalized obesity by over-eating? Or in those cases, often these textbooks pre-World War II were titled obesity and leanness because they were looking at cases that today we would call anorexia and assuming that that also wasn't an under-eating problem. It was some problem of how the fat tissue was regulated. So why do we believe this? And let's look at a little physics here, okay? And this is the reason.
cues.zh: 那你凭什么会认为可以用吃得过多来解释全身性肥胖呢？在二战前的那些教科书里，书名往往叫做《肥胖与消瘦》，因为他们当时观察的那些今天会被称为厌食症的病例，并认为那同样不是吃得少的问题，而是脂肪组织调节机制出了问题。那么我们为什么会相信这种说法呢？咱们来看看一点物理学知识，好吗？原因就在这里。

cues.en: We believe it because of the first law of thermodynamics. Every time somebody like me makes this point for the past 56 years, you get accused of not believing that thermodynamics holds for human beings. I had one of the high points in my life. I was on the Larry King show after good calories, bad calories came out. And they had Jillian Michaels, the trainer from The Biggest Loser, come on. And she gave me a lecture on the laws of thermodynamics on national television. And I have a physics degree from Harvard.
cues.zh: 我们相信它，是因为热力学第一定律。在过去的56年里，每当像我这样的人提出这个观点，就会被指责不相信热力学适用于人类。我人生中最戏剧性的时刻之一，是在《Good Calories, Bad Calories》出版后上了《Larry King》节目，他们请来了《The Biggest Loser》的教练 Jillian Michaels，她在全国电视观众面前给我上了一堂热力学定律课。而我可是有哈佛物理学学位的。

cues.en: I was a lousy student, but it was definitely, I literally, I'm sitting next to, you know, I just, I didn't respond. If you watch the show, it's on, you can Google it. I didn't know what to say. I mean, how do I respond to this? So let me give you the thermodynamics. It's pretty simple. First law of thermodynamics, it's a law of energy conservation. It says change in energy in a system, this is the simplest possible way to put it. It's equal to the energy in minus energy out. All it's saying is you can't create energy from any, you know,
cues.zh: 虽然我当时是个糟糕的学生，但那绝对是……我当时就坐在旁边，简直无言以对。如果你去看那个节目，网上能搜到，我当时都不知道该说什么，我到底该怎么回应这种事？所以让我来给大家讲讲热力学，其实很简单。热力学第一定律就是能量守恒定律，它指出一个系统的能量变化——这是最简单的表述方式——等于摄入能量减去消耗能量。它无非是在说，能量不可能凭空产生。

cues.en: thin air. So if a system gets bigger, delta E goes up, then it's got to take in more energy than it expands. And if a system gets smaller, it's got to expend more energy than it takes in. For our sake, we'll make delta E the fat mass. E in is energy consumed. E out, energy expended. So change in fat mass equals energy consumed minus energy expended. And the problem, the fundamental problem, and it's almost unbelievable to me.
cues.zh: 凭空产生。因此，如果一个系统变大，也就是 ΔE 增加，那它摄入的能量必然大于消耗的能量；如果一个系统变小，它消耗的能量必然大于摄入的能量。在我们的讨论里，把 ΔE 看作脂肪量，E_in 是摄入能量，E_out 是消耗能量。所以脂肪量的变化等于摄入能量减去消耗能量。而问题在于，那个根本性的问题——这对我来说几乎难以置信。

cues.en: is that there's no arrow of causality here, okay? And by that, I mean it doesn't say in any way if energy, you know, energy consumed greater than energy expended causes change of fat mass. It just says this is the way the universe is. If a system gets bigger, it takes in more energy than it expands. And if a system gets smaller, it takes in less. It says nothing about what causes it. And to understand that, a metaphor I could use, like, let's assume I was asking the question, why is this room crowded right now?
cues.zh: 这里面根本没有因果之箭，明白吗？我的意思是，它完全没说是摄入能量大于消耗能量导致了脂肪量的改变。它只是陈述了宇宙的客观规律：如果一个系统变大了，它吸收的能量必然多于释放的；如果变小了，吸收的就更少。它根本没解释背后的原因。为了理解这点，打个比方，假设我问：为什么现在这个房间这么挤？

cues.en: Okay? And it's a similar, when we're talking about fat mass, we want to know, why is there so much energy accumulated in the fat mass? And I want to ask the question, why is there so much energy accumulated in this room in the form of people? So you asked me, Gary, why is it crowded? And I say, well, because more people entered than left. Right? Have I told you anything meaningful at all about why this? I mean, of course more people entered than left, but why is it crowded? And then I say, okay, well, look, if more people entered than leave,
cues.zh: 懂吧？这很类似，当我们谈论脂肪量时，我们想知道的是：为什么脂肪组织里积累了这么多能量？而我想问的是：为什么这个房间里以“人”的形式聚集了这么多能量？如果你问我：“Gary，为什么这里这么挤？”我回答：“因为进来的人比出去的人多呗。”对吧？那我说了任何有价值的原因吗？进来的人当然比出去的多，但这怎么能解释为什么挤呢？然后我又说：“行吧，你看，要是进来的人比出去的多，

cues.en: It's got to get crowded, right? And I still haven't told you anything, meaning this is what logicians would call, I forget the word vacuous. It's equivalent as saying, why did you get fat because you took in more energy than you expended? Well, of course I took in more energy than I expended. I got fat, but why did I get fat? And then you just turn around and say, well, if you take in more energy than you expend,
cues.zh: 这儿肯定得挤起来，对吧？”但我依然什么都没解释，逻辑学家会称之为——我想想那个词，空洞无物。这就像是在说：“你为什么变胖？因为你摄入的能量比消耗的多。”废话，我当然摄入得比消耗的多，我都变胖了，但究竟是什么让我变胖的呢？结果你转头又说：“呃，如果你摄入的比消耗的多，

cues.en: There's no arrow of causality. There's nothing meaningful here. This is a mistake that was made occasionally prior to the Second World War. It became ubiquitous after the Second World War. Whenever we tell someone you got fat because you over ate, you are misinterpreting the laws of thermodynamics on an eighth grade mathematics level. And the more I talk about it, the more it's almost unbelievable that this ever happened. And yet it did.
cues.zh: 这里根本没有因果之箭。这种说法毫无意义。二战前大家偶尔还会犯这种错误，二战后它却变得无处不在。每当我们对别人说“你变胖是因为你吃多了”，我们其实都是在用初二的数学水平曲解热力学定律。我越讨论这个，越觉得这种事情能发生简直匪夷所思。然而它确实发生了。

cues.en: And so there's another way you could play with these thermodynamics, and for this I owe a University of Washington grad student named Sonya Trejo, who said, what happens if you just start transposing elements? So how about this? Instead of, you know, we had delta E over here and E out over here, how about if we say energy out is equal to energy and minus delta E? So now the energy expended is equal to energy consumed minus change in fat mass, okay? So if fat mass gets bigger...
cues.zh: 所以你还可以用另一种方式来推演这些热力学公式，这多亏了华盛顿大学一位叫 Sonya Trejo 的研究生，她说：“要是把公式里的项做个移项会怎样？”那我们试试看：与其把 ΔE 放在这边、输出能量放在那边，不如写成“输出能量等于输入能量减去 ΔE”？这样一来，消耗的能量就等于摄入的能量减去脂肪量的改变，对吧？那么如果脂肪量增加了……

cues.en: But we don't know why. We're working on that. And the person doesn't eat anymore, then energy expenditure has to go down. So you look at it this way, and an increase in fat mass causes sedentary behavior. If fat mass gets smaller, energy expended has to go up. So if somebody's losing weight, they have to get more physically active. Or how about this one? We just do a little more transposing, and we end up with energy N equals delta E plus energy L. So the energy we eat
cues.zh: 但我们还不知道为什么，这还在研究中。如果这个人没有多吃，那能量消耗就必须降下来。所以换这个角度看，脂肪量增加反而导致了久坐不动的行为。如果脂肪量减少了，消耗的能量就必须增加，也就是说如果有人在减肥，他就必然会变得更爱运动。或者再看这个：我们再做一次移项，得到“输入能量等于 ΔE 加上输出能量”。也就是说，我们吃进去的能量，

cues.en: is equal to change in fat mass plus energy expended. Let's assume change in fat mass is fixed by biology. And if you read the New York Times today, there was an article about that. An energy expenditure goes up because I just told you to work out what's going to happen to energy consumed. It has to go up. You're going to get hungry. You will work up an appetite. This used to be something that everyone believed in the 1960s and beyond. It used to be this term working up an appetite.
cues.zh: 等于脂肪量的改变加上消耗的能量。假设脂肪量的改变是由生物机理决定的——如果你今天读了《纽约时报》，上面刚好有篇相关文章——而由于我刚刚让你去健身，你的能量消耗增加了，那么摄入的能量会怎样？它必然得增加。你会变饿，你会“运动出胃口”。在 20 世纪 60 年代及更早的时候，这是人尽皆知的常识，以前经常有“运动出食欲”这种说法。

cues.en: So it used to be, if you worked out, you worked up an appetite. Now if you work out, you're supposed to lose weight, and energy consumed is supposed to stay fixed. But there's no guarantee this will happen. So here's the alternative hypothesis. This is a way that the pre-World War II Europeans thought about it.
cues.zh: 以前常说，运动会让人胃口大开。现在却说，运动能减肥，而且摄入的能量应该保持不变。但这并不能保证一定会发生。所以这里有另一种假说。这是二战前欧洲人的一种思路。

cues.en: They said, started from first principles, okay, obesity is a disorder of excess fat accumulation. So today you'll read obesity is a sort of positive energy balance, or obesity is an energy balance problem, and those are assumptions. They just started at the beginning, having too much fat is a sort of having too much fat. Okay, so it's not energy balance, it's not overeating, it's not sedentary behavior. And if you ask it this way, the next question you're likely to ask, which we'll get to, is what regulates fat accumulation?
cues.zh: 他们从第一性原理出发，认为肥胖是一种脂肪过度堆积的病症。而今天你会读到肥胖是某种正能量平衡，或者肥胖是能量平衡问题，这些都只是假设。他们直接从本质切入：脂肪过多就是脂肪过多的问题。好，所以这不是能量平衡问题，不是暴饮暴食，也不是久坐不动。如果你这样思考，接下来很可能会问一个问题——我们稍后会讲到——到底是什么在调控脂肪堆积？

cues.en: Because what we know is there's too much fat. Like if I was standing in here with Yao Ming, who's seven feet six inches tall, and we want to know why he grew to be seven foot six, we wouldn't care that he was in positive energy balance. We would want to know what regulates growth, right? So we want to know what regulates growth. So by this hypothesis, overeating and inactivity are compensatory effects, they're not causes. And the way it was put to me by several different individuals doing animal research, so we don't get fat because we overeat.
cues.zh: 因为我们确切知道的是脂肪过剩了。就像如果我和姚明站在这里，他身高2米26，如果我们想知道他为什么能长到2米26，我们不会去在乎他是不是处于正能量平衡。我们会想知道是什么调控了生长，对吧？所以我们想知道是什么调控了生长。根据这个假说，暴饮暴食和缺乏运动只是代偿效应，并不是根本原因。几位从事动物研究的学者向我这样解释：我们不是因为吃得过多才变胖的。

cues.en: We overeat because our fat tissue is accumulating excess fat. Overeating is a given. If you're getting fatter, you have to take in more calories than you consume. But we're saying the positive energy balance is an effect. Here's a way to see it. This comes from, again, straight out of the pre-World War II text, although the child is mine. I use these photos because he's so cute. He was.
cues.zh: 我们吃得多，是因为我们的脂肪组织在过度堆积脂肪。吃得过多是必然现象。如果你在变胖，你摄入的热量肯定多于消耗的热量。但我们的观点是，正能量平衡只是结果。我们可以这样来看。这同样直接来源于二战前的文献，虽然照片里是我的孩子。我用这些照片是因为他太可爱了，至少曾经是。

cues.en: Here he was, one year old, 20 pounds, 2006. Here he is, 2009, 45 pounds. He's gained 25 pounds in three years. He's been in positive energy balance. He has over eaten. He's taken in more calories and expended, but he did not grow because he over ate. He over ate because he was growing. He grew because he was secreting growth hormone.
cues.zh: 这是他2006年一岁时的样子，20磅。这是2009年，45磅。他在三年里长了25磅。他一直处于正能量平衡中。他吃得很多。他摄入的热量超过了消耗的热量，但他并不是因为吃得多才长大的。他吃得多是因为他在长身体。他长身体是因为他在分泌生长激素。

cues.en: And the growth hormone sparked his tissues to grow, muscle, organs, fat, bone, and he had to take in more calories and he expended to fuel that growth. And if he wasn't growing fast enough, we might have even given him more growth hormone to speed his growth, in which point that would have created even more positive energy balance. Here's a gruesome analogy, cancer. Here's a tumor.
cues.zh: 生长激素刺激了他的组织生长，肌肉、器官、脂肪、骨骼，他必须摄入多于消耗的热量来支撑这种生长。如果他长得不够快，我们甚至可能给他注射更多生长激素来加速生长，到那时这会引发更显著的正能量平衡。这里有个可怕的类比：癌症。这是一个肿瘤。

cues.en: could barely see it, then it's growing at day 10, it's growing at day 20, it's bigger and bigger. This tumor is in positive energy balance, nobody cares. We care if we want to starve it to death, but that's a given. Like just if we don't want this room to get crowded, we'll shut the doors before anyone comes in. But what we care about is what genes, what hormones are disruptive that drive the growth because the positive energy balance is an effect.
cues.zh: 起初几乎看不见，到了第10天在长大，第20天还在长，越变越大。这个肿瘤处于能量正平衡状态，但没人在乎这个。要是我们想饿死它，我们才会在乎，但这显而易见。就像如果我们不想让这间屋子太挤，只要在人进来前把门关上就行。但我们真正关心的是，究竟是哪些基因、哪些激素失调推动了这种生长，因为能量正平衡只是一个结果。

cues.en: And in every other example in nature, positive energy balance is always an effect of growth, not the other way around. So this was a German-Austrian hypothesis prior to World War II. It was known as the lipophilia hypothesis. I'll explain that in a second.
cues.zh: 在自然界的任何其他例子中，能量正平衡始终是生长的结果，而不是原因。这就是二战前德奥学者提出的一种假说。它被称为亲脂性假说。我马上会解释这一点。

cues.en: Primary proponents were Gustav von Bergmann, who was a German specialist in internal medicine. Today, the highest award in the German Association of Internal Medicine is the Gustav von Bergmann Award. And then Julius Bauer, who was a geneticist and endocrinologist at the University of Vienna. Bauer was very famous in Austria. If you have any molecular biology or genetics friends in Austria, email them and say, have you ever heard of Julius Bauer? And they'll probably say, oh, yeah, absolutely.
cues.zh: 主要支持者是 Gustav von Bergmann，他是德国的内科医学专家。如今，德国胸腹内科学会的最高荣誉就是 Gustav von Bergmann 奖。另一位是 Julius Bauer，他是维也纳大学的遗传学家和内分泌学家。Bauer 在奥地利非常出名。如果你在奥地利有做分子生物学或遗传学的朋友，发邮件问他们：“你听说过 Julius Bauer 吗？”他们大概率会说：“噢，当然听过。”

cues.en: And the theory was more or less fully accepted in Europe by 1940. This comes from the 1940 textbook. And the problem was, 1940 was a bad year for Europe. So the German and Austrian medical research communities evaporate, unlike in physics where we embraced all the European physicists who got chased out of Europe because we had atomic bombs to build and hydrogen bombs and a Cold War to fight. In medicine and public health, we didn't.
cues.zh: 到了1940年，这个理论在欧洲基本上已被完全接受。这出自1940年的一本教科书。但问题是，1940年对欧洲来说是个糟糕的年份。德奥两国的医学研究界彻底消亡，与物理学界截然不同——当时我们接纳了所有被驱逐出欧洲的物理学家，因为我们得造原子弹、氢弹，还要打冷战。但在医学和公共卫生领域，我们没有这么做。

cues.en: So Julius Bauer ended up working in Hollywood, California for the Hospital of Medical Evangelists and publishing articles that just said Julius Bauer, Hollywood, California. And nobody took his work seriously, although his son became dean of the USC Medical School. So here's lipophilia in a nutshell. The idea is...
cues.zh: 因此 Julius Bauer 最终流落到加州好莱坞，在 Hospital of Medical Evangelists 工作，发表文章时的署名也只写着 Julius Bauer，加州好莱坞。再也没人把他的研究当回事，尽管他的儿子后来当上了 USC 医学院的院长。简而言之，亲脂性假说是这样的。其核心观点是……

cues.en: Lipophilia means love of fat. And the way these people saw it is that some tissues are more or less predisposed to accumulate fat in the same way that, you know, you can think of it, we grow hair in some places and not in others. And we get fat in some places and not in others. So we don't tend to get fat on our foreheads or the back of our hands, but we put on fat in our guts, under our chins. And so they said maybe...
cues.zh: 亲脂性字面意思是“对脂肪的喜好”。这些学者认为，某些组织或多或少天生更容易堆积脂肪，就如同你可以想象的那样，我们只在某些部位长毛发，而在其他部位不长。我们的脂肪也只长在特定部位。比如我们的额头或手背往往不会长脂肪，但在肚子上、下巴底下却会长。所以他们提出，或许……

cues.en: You know, fat is just like hair. And so some people are hairier than others, just like some people are fatter than others. You know, when men start losing their hair, we don't accuse them of under-eating because they're losing weight. We know that there's, you know, a lot of different issues involved. So Bauer put it like this. He said, like a malignant tumor, like the fetus, the uterus or the breast of a pregnant woman, the abnormal lipophilic tissue seizes on food stuffs, even in the case of under-nutrition.
cues.zh: 脂肪就跟毛发一样。正如有些人毛发比别人更浓密，有些人也比别人更胖。当男性开始脱发时，我们不会因为他体重减轻就指责他是吃太少了。我们知道这背后涉及很多不同的因素。所以 Bauer 这样表述过。他说：就像恶性肿瘤，就像孕妇体内的胎儿、子宫或乳房一样，异常的亲脂性组织即便在营养不良的情况下，也会强行攫取养分。

cues.en: It maintains its stock and may increase it, independent of the requirements of the organism, sort of anarchy exists. The adipose tissue lives for itself and does not fit into the precisely regulated management of the organism. And this phrase, even in the case of undernutrition, begins to tell us why these women could get obese in a population where their children are starving, because it didn't matter how little food there was. If there was something driving their accumulation of fat, they were going to get fat anyway.
cues.zh: 它维持着自身的储备，甚至可能增加，完全不受身体需求的限制，就像处于某种无政府状态。脂肪组织只顾自己生存，不受机体精密调控的管辖。而“即使在营养不良的情况下”这句话，开始向我们揭示为什么在孩子们都在挨饿的人群中，这些妇女却会发胖，因为食物再少也无关紧要。只要有某种因素在促使她们囤积脂肪，她们横竖都会胖起来。

cues.en: So when you look at animal models of obesity, which you can, what you'll find, what I found, is they'll fall into two categories. Either, well, let me just explain. If you have an animal model of obesity, how do you want to test what's driving it? Like a genetic model, a surgical model, you could lesion, the ventral media, go hypothalamus, veratin, it'll get obese and eat voraciously. So you'll see voracious eating and obesity, and you want to know which causes which.
cues.zh: 所以当你去研究肥胖的动物模型时——这是可行的——你会发现，我发现它们可以分为两类。或者，好吧，我来解释一下。如果你有一个肥胖的动物模型，你打算怎么测试其背后的诱因？比如基因模型、手术模型，你可以损伤下丘脑腹内侧核，它就会发胖并且暴饮暴食。于是你看到了贪食和肥胖，你就会想知道究竟是谁导致了谁。

cues.en: Did the dysregulation of fat tissue cause what's called hyperphasia? Or did the hyperphasia cause the accumulation of fat? So what you do is you just do the experiment, then you put the animals on a diet and you see whether they get fat anyway. Okay? And what you'll find for every animal model of obesity is they will get obese anyway, even if you put them on a diet. You know, you can, in some cases, starving, like...
cues.zh: 是脂肪组织的失调导致了所谓的食欲亢进吗？还是食欲亢进导致了脂肪囤积？所以你要做的就是做这个实验，给动物节食，看看它们是否仍然会变胖。明白吗？而你在每一个肥胖动物模型中都会发现，即便限制饮食，它们依然会变胖。在某些情况下，你甚至可以让它们挨饿，比如……

cues.en: There's a genetic strain of mice that M.R.C. Greenwood studied in the early 1980s when she put these animals on a diet from the moment they were weaned, and they became more obese, they became fatter than their lean control, than their genetic controls, even though they were on a diet their whole life. They actually weighed less. Their organs were smaller, their muscle tissue was smaller, and they had more fat. And the fact their drive to accumulate fat was...
cues.zh: M.R.C. Greenwood 在 20 世纪 80 年代初研究过一种基因品系小鼠，她从这些小鼠断奶那一刻起就对它们进行节食，尽管终身节食，它们却变得更肥胖，比那些消瘦的对照组，也就是基因对照组还要胖。实际上它们的体重更轻。它们的内脏更小，肌肉组织更少，但脂肪却更多。事实上，它们囤积脂肪的动力……

cues.en: You know, in order to do that, they cannibalize their organs and their brain. And Jean Maier, a Tufts nutritionist who played a large role in this, usually to the detriment of society. The way he put it, he studied the genetic strain of mice. He said these mice will make fat out of their food under the most unlikely circumstances, even when half-starved. Okay? So it's not that these mice got fat.
cues.zh: 为了囤积脂肪，它们甚至不惜蚕食自己的器官和大脑。塔夫茨大学的营养学家 Jean Mayer 在这一领域影响深远，虽然通常带来的是负面影响。按他的说法——他也研究过这种基因品系小鼠——他说这些小鼠在极不可能的情况下，哪怕处于半饥饿状态，也能把食物转化为脂肪。明白吗？所以并不是这些小鼠变胖……

cues.en: because they ate too much. They got fat if you let them eat anything, basically. And we're going to propose again that the same thing's happening in humans. So here's some obvious questions. Why vertical growth but not horizontal? When we look at children, we know that overeating is the effect, growth is the cause. Why animals but not men? In animal models of obesity, when you break a gene, you intervene surgically. There are even dietary models.
cues.zh: 是因为它们吃得太多。基本上只要你给它们吃任何东西，它们就会发胖。我们再次提出，同样的情况也发生在人类身上。那么这里有几个显而易见的问题：为什么是纵向生长（长高）而不是横向生长（长胖）？当我们观察儿童时，我们知道多吃是结果，生长才是原因。为什么动物如此，人类就不是？在动物肥胖模型中，当你破坏一个基因，或者进行手术干预，甚至还有饮食诱导模型。

cues.en: What you're doing is disregulating the fat tissue. You're not making the animals eat too much. And then the question, you know, if obesity is sort of excess fat accumulation, what regulates fat accumulation? So here's a regulation of fat. At a positive one-on-one, if you learn this, you'll know more than your doctors do. By the way, what gets me?
cues.zh: 你所做的是扰乱脂肪组织的调节，而不是让动物吃得过多。那么问题来了，如果肥胖是过量脂肪的积累，那又是什么在调节脂肪积累呢？这就是脂肪的调节机制。这是脂肪组织的基础知识，学懂这个，你懂的就比你的医生还多了。顺便说一句，让我感到不可思议的是……

cues.en: is that, again, it's 2011. I lecture in medical schools. I lecture at obesity research centers. And I'm telling them, it's like I'm telling them something new. I mean, they all learned this in medical school, but they forgot it. But when it comes to the relevance of obesity, or why we get fat, the idea that your fat tissue is regulated and has anything to say about this is considered radical and quackish. And the point I'm making is, any other growth
cues.zh: 现在都2011年了，我在医学院讲课，在肥胖研究中心讲课，可我讲这些时，他们却像是在听什么新鲜事一样。我是说，他们医学院里都学过这个，但全忘了。可一旦涉及肥胖的成因，或者我们为什么会发胖，认为脂肪组织受到调节并在其中起主导作用的观点，居然会被视作激进甚至江湖骗术。而我的核心观点是，任何其他的生长……

cues.en: Like I said, from cancer to height to anything, all you're going to care about is what hormones, what enzymes are driving growth. So let's care about it here, too. And so the same year that the American Physiological Society put out its high-fat diet, it's a handbook of adipose tissue metabolism saying carbohydrates drive insulin, drive fat.
