cues.zh: 既然饮食脂肪会导致心脏病，可别忘了我刚才说过，低碳水饮食其实就是高脂肪饮食。就在同一年，美国生理学会出版了脂肪组织代谢手册，指出碳水化合物驱动胰岛素，进而转化为脂肪。这相当于把500页的手册浓缩成短短一句话。

cues.en: The New York Times was already panning carbide low carb diets. New diet decried by nutritionist, dangers are seen in low carbohydrate intake. Some of the nation's top nutrition experts are concerned with the new popularity of the low carb reducing diet, which one of them calls nonsense, because you don't have to restrict calories, because it's not about calories. And another compares to mass murder. This is Jean Maier, who was the most influential nutritionist in the country, went on to become president of Tufts University.
cues.zh: 而《纽约时报》当时已经在痛批低碳水饮食了。营养学家谴责新饮食法，称低碳水摄入存在危险。全国顶尖营养专家对低碳水减肥法的流行深感担忧，其中一位称其纯属胡扯，因为这种方法不用限制卡路里，重点根本不在卡路里上。另一位甚至将其比作大屠杀。这位就是让·马耶尔，当时全美最有影响力的营养学家，后来还成了塔夫茨大学的校长。

cues.en: mass murder because you're giving people high fat diet. So the science says carbohydrates driving insulin is driving fat, cut the carbs out, the nutritionists are saying, you can't do that, you're going to kill people. And that's how we've seen it ever since. And you get to the point by the 1980s where you end up with the food guide pyramid because we believe fats are fattening and we believe red meat causes colon cancer or God knows what. We're going to tell an entire nation to eat bread, cereal, rice, pasta.
cues.zh: 无异于大规模谋杀，因为你让人吃高脂饮食。科学明明表明碳水化合物刺激胰岛素，进而促进脂肪堆积，应该减少碳水；而营养学家却说，万万不可，这会害死人的。从那以后局面一直如此。到了20世纪80年代，甚至出台了膳食指南金字塔，因为我们坚信脂肪催人发胖，坚信红肉会导致结肠癌或天晓得什么病。于是我们告诫全国民众去多吃面包、谷物、米饭和意面。

cues.en: Sweets, weirdly enough, get a free pass because they're non-fatening. So coke, Pepsi, soba, iced tea, snapples. There was actually a theory in the 1980s you could drink as much. You could eat as much any food you want if it didn't have fat in it. Because if it didn't have fat in it, you couldn't put fat on. So just to wrap up, I've already gone too long, as I always do.
cues.zh: 令人费解的是，甜食反而被网开一面，因为它们不含脂肪。可乐、百事、苏打水、冰茶、Snapple饮料都无所谓了。80年代甚至有一种理论认为，任何食物只要不含脂肪，你爱喝多少就喝多少，爱吃多少就吃多少。因为只要食物没有脂肪，你就不会长脂肪。总而言之，我又讲超时了，老毛病了。

cues.en: I started off asking the question, why were these populations fat? Ralph Richards in 1973. Most third world countries have a high carbohydrate intake as their economic dependence is predominantly agricultural with a heavy dependence on non-dairy produces. It is conceivable that the ready availability of starch in preference to animal protein contributing as it must the main caloric requirements of these populations leads to increased lipogenesis and the development of obesity.
cues.zh: 我一开始提出的问题是，为什么这些人群会发胖？Ralph Richards在1973年指出：大多数第三世界国家碳水摄入量很高，因为其经济主要依赖农业，极度倚重非奶制品农作物。不难想象，淀粉极易获取而动物蛋白匮乏，淀粉必然构成了这些人群的主要热量来源，从而导致脂肪生成增加并引发肥胖。

cues.en: In this country, we took the conventional wisdom that carbohydrates make you fat, and over the course of 20 years, from 1960 to 1980s, turned it into the conventional wisdom that you grew up with, that carbohydrates are heart-healthy diet foods, and it's the fat that makes you fat. And that's why there's an obesity epidemic. I mean, surely the sugar and high fructose corn syrup didn't help. And that's why we all have trouble struggling with our weight, because the approach we use to cure it
cues.zh: 而在我们国家，我们抛弃了“碳水让人发胖”的传统共识，在1960到1980这20年间，将其扭曲成了你们耳濡目染的观念：碳水化合物有益心脏健康，是减肥食品，而脂肪才是致胖元凶。这就是肥胖蔓延的原因。当然，糖和高果糖玉米糖浆也难辞其咎。这也是为什么我们大家都在为体重苦苦挣扎，因为我们用来减肥的方法——

cues.en: eat less, exercise more, and eat low-fat diets is exactly the wrong thing. Basic question is, I'll phrase it the way it's usually phrased, what about those Southeast Asians who live on low-fat, high-carb diets and don't get fat? And one of the fundamental issues here, and actually this is partially why I wrote the Sugar Store in the New York Times a couple weeks ago, basically in the beginning I showed you populations that ate high-carb diets that were very poor and were fat.
cues.zh: 少吃、多动、低脂饮食——完全背道而驰。一个基本的问题是，我就按大家常问的方式说吧，那些吃低脂高碳饮食却不发胖的东南亚人，又是怎么回事呢？这其中的核心问题之一，其实也是我几周前在《纽约时报》发表关于糖的文章的部分原因。一开始我向大家展示了一些极度贫困、吃高碳水饮食却很胖的人群。

cues.en: And then there are populations, the Japanese, the Koreans, the Chinese, elsewhere, the Kitavans, who eat high carb diets and aren't fat. And what's the difference? Or is it not the carbohydrates? And again, what I'm saying is the high glycemic, high refined carbs and the sugars. And if you look at the populations that don't get fat, they eat effectively very little sugar. So the Japanese, for instance, in the 1960s were eating the amount of sugar that we were eating in the 1860s.
cues.zh: 但还有像日本人、韩国人、中国人，以及基塔瓦人等其他群体，他们也吃高碳水饮食，却并不胖。区别何在？难道问题不在碳水本身？我想强调的是，问题在于高升糖、精加工的碳水以及糖类。如果去观察那些不发胖的人群，他们吃下的糖其实非常少。以日本人为例，他们在1960年代的吃糖量，仅仅相当于我们在1860年代的水平。

cues.en: The Katabans eat virtually no sugar. The way the research will talk about it is these nations don't have sweet tooths, sweet teeth. So my answer would be, and this is one of the reasons why I believe it may be necessary, sugar may be necessary to trigger this, and that's what the biochemistry, the science suggests today. And once sugar's in the diet, all things. One of the interesting things,
cues.zh: 卡塔巴人几乎不吃糖。研究人员通常会说，这些民族并不爱吃甜食。所以我的回答是——这也是我认为糖可能是必需诱因的原因之一，目前的生物化学和科学证据也指向这一点。而一旦饮食中有了糖，一切都会改变。有趣的事情之一是，

cues.en: One of the suggestions I made in the New York Times Magazine article was that sugar could actually be the fundamental cause of cancer. So remember, you want to explain observations. And one observation is that Japanese women in Japan have, you know,
cues.zh: 我在《纽约时报杂志》的文章中提出的观点之一，就是糖实际上可能是导致癌症的根本原因。请记住，我们总想解释观察到的现象。其中一个现象是，生活在日本的日本女性，

cues.en: very little breast cancer, and then they come to the United States, and within two generations you have virtually the same breast cancer rates as any other population. And what could explain this? There's something happening here that's causing it, or there's something that's preventing it in Japan. It's a common observation throughout the world, and one of the things I would suggest is they come here and more sugar gets into their diets.
cues.zh: 乳腺癌发病率极低，但当她们来到美国后，只需两代人的时间，她们的乳腺癌发病率就几乎与其他人群无异。这该如何解释？要么是这里的某种因素导致了这种情况，要么是日本本土有某种预防因素。这在全世界都是个普遍观察到的现象，而我认为原因之一是，她们来到这里后，饮食中摄入了更多的糖。

cues.en: And the reason they don't have it there is because there's such little sugar, they don't have insulin resistance, and they don't have all these triggers. So no hypothesis to me would be it's a sugar. You could evoke other hypotheses, the length of time that the refined carb, in this case, white rice or the grain, had been in the population. But the sugar is the thing that would seem the most obvious. Hi. I have a couple of personal questions. Do you agree to not answer them?
cues.zh: 而在日本发病率低的原因是糖摄入量极低，她们没有胰岛素抵抗，也没有这所有的诱因。所以对我来说，最明显的假说就是糖。你当然也可以提出其他假说，比如该人群食用精制碳水（在这里是精米或谷物）的历史长短。但糖看起来是最显而易见的原因。你好，我有几个私人问题。你可以选择不回答吗？

cues.en: One is, do you follow this diet that you recommend? Yeah. And what is your waist size in inches? My waist size in inches? Well, the question is, see, this is always one of the mistakes people make in life. I mean, I'm OK here, OK? Basically, I have the same body I had when I was in college. I was a defensive tackle at Harvard. I was a bad one. Actually, I'm 20 pounds less than I was then. But when you're trying to be a defensive lineman, you're trying to be as heavy as you can.
cues.zh: 一个是，你自己遵循你推荐的这种饮食法吗？遵循。还有，你的腰围是多少英寸？我的腰围多少英寸？嗯，问题在于，你看，这正是人们在生活中常犯的错误之一。我是说，我还行吧，对吧？基本上，我的体型跟读大学时差不多。我当时是哈佛大学的防守绊锋。打得挺差的。实际上，我现在比那时还轻了20磅。但当你试图成为一名防守锋线球员时，你会尽可能让自己更重。

cues.en: It is actually not important how big I am on my diet. What would be important is how much bigger I would be if I added carbohydrates back into the diet. That would be the relevant. I could starve myself. Actually, my good example is my brother. My brother's a professor of mathematics at Harvard. He's a very smart guy. He was always lean, and I was always thick.
cues.zh: 按照我的饮食法，我有多胖其实并不重要。重要的是，如果我把碳水化合物重新加回饮食中，我会变得多胖。那才是有意义的对照。我可以把自己饿瘦。其实，我哥哥就是个很好的例子。我哥哥是哈佛大学的数学教授。他非常聪明。他从小就很瘦，而我一直很壮。

cues.en: He was always, you could see, when he was seven, you could see his muscles and his veins, and you could see my pot belly. And when we grew up, we both ate all the food we could. As a matter of fact, we ate as fast as we could, because if I didn't eat fast, he'd eat it first. He was more physically active. Well, he wasn't. He could run longer distances. I could starve myself to death and never look like my brother. I will die of starvation before I am as lean as my brother is, because we are physiologic. We partition fuel differently.
cues.zh: 他一直都是，你一眼就能看出来，他七岁的时候，就能看清他的肌肉和血管，而你只能看到我的大肚腩。我们长大时，俩人都尽可能多吃。事实上，我们吃得都极快，因为如果我吃得不快，就被他先吃光了。他身体更活跃吗？其实也没有。他只是更能长跑。我就算把自己饿死，也绝不可能像我哥那么瘦。在我能达到我哥那么瘦之前，我早就饿死了，因为我们的生理机制不同。我们对能量燃料的分配机制截然不同。

cues.en: But the question is, what would happen if I added carbs back to my diet? Would my waist size be bigger? Right now, I'm 6 foot 2, 220 pounds. My waist size is probably 35. When I was in college, I was 6 foot 2, 220 pounds. Actually, and my waist size was 35. In between, I was heavier. Never likely to be obese, although because I'm a big guy, my BMI could go over 30.
cues.zh: 但问题是，如果我重新在饮食中加入碳水会怎样？我的腰围会变粗吗？我现在身高 6 英尺 2 英寸，体重 220 磅，腰围大概是 35。我上大学时也是 6 英尺 2 英寸，220 磅，腰围也是 35。这期间我曾更胖过，虽然不至于算肥胖，但因为我骨架大，BMI 确实可能超过 30。

cues.en: You know for me Well, it might kill me. That's the question the question is not whether I'm heavy or lighter the question is am I going to die? Sooner because I eat a lot of saturated fat and one thing I don't have time to do in this lecture I do in another lecture if you actually look at the clinical trials which compare high fat diets to low fat diets
cues.zh: 对我来说，这可能会要了我的命。这就是关键问题，问题不在于我是胖了还是瘦了，而在于：我会不会因为吃了大量饱和脂肪而英年早逝？由于时间关系，我无法在这场讲座中展开，但我会在另一场讲座中讲到：如果你去看看对比高脂饮食和低脂饮食的临床试验……

cues.en: The way these have been done over the past decade is basically putting people, randomizing people to an Atkins diet, which is high fat, high saturated fat, eat as much as you want, and a low fat American Heart Association, low calorie restricted diet. So one diet, you cut fat, you cut saturated fat, you cut calories, so you're eating like, you know, skinless chicken breast and lettuce. And the other diet, you can eat as much as you want, so you're eating, you know, eggs and bacon for breakfast and, you know, meat and...
cues.zh: 过去十年里，这些试验的做法基本是将受试者随机分配到阿特金斯饮食组和美国心脏协会推荐的低脂低卡饮食组；前者是高脂、高饱和脂肪且不限进食量的，后者则是限制热量的。在一种饮食中，你要少吃脂肪、少吃饱和脂肪并限制卡路里，基本上只能吃去皮鸡胸肉和生菜；而在另一种饮食中，你想吃多少就吃多少，早餐可以吃培根煎蛋，还有肉类和……

cues.en: double cheeseburgers without the bun and the sort of iconic Atkins thing. And nobody really sticks these diets the way they should, but when the trials are done, what you find is not only the people on the high fat diet, ad lib and a meat as much as you like diet, way less, even though they're told they could eat as much as they want, their heart disease risk factors, profiles improve. And this is what actually got me into this subject.
cues.zh: 不带面包胚的双层芝士汉堡，也就是阿特金斯饮食的标志性吃法。虽然没人能真正严格按要求坚持这些饮食，但试验结束后的发现是：那些采取高脂、肉类随意吃饮食的人，不仅体重更轻了——尽管他们被告知想吃多少就吃多少——而且他们的心脏病风险指标也改善了。这正是我深入研究这一课题的契机。

cues.en: When I was writing this story for the New York Times Magazine in 2002, I found five of these trials that had been done and not yet published yet. And again, if we say let's pretend this is a science, you know, we have a hypothesis. We have two of them. One of them is that saturated fat causes heart disease, and one of them is that if you eat more, you'll get fat. So now I'm going to put you on a diet that says you can eat as much as you want and as much saturated fat as you want, and I recommend you do it. Our hypothesis predicts that you will
cues.zh: 2002 年我为《New York Times Magazine》撰写这篇报道时，发现了五项已经完成但尚未发表的此类试验。如果把这当成一门科学，我们手头有两个假说：一个是饱和脂肪会导致心脏病，另一个是吃得越多就会越胖。现在我让你执行一种饮食，你可以想吃多少就吃多少，想吃多少饱和脂肪就吃多少，甚至我还建议你这么吃。按照我们的假说预测，你应该会……

cues.en: gain weight, and get heart disease, and instead what happened in these trials is these people lose weight, and their heart disease risk factors improve. Across the board, everything improves, okay? So the question then becomes, maybe our hypothesis is wrong. You answered, already answered my question to some extent, you answered the last one, but clarified for my personal, I mean, in the beginning of your talk, you,
cues.zh: 体重增加并患上心脏病。但这些试验中实际发生的情况是，这些人反而瘦了，而且他们的心脏病风险指标也有所改善。全方位地、各项指标都改善了，对吧？那么问题就来了：也许我们的假说根本就是错的。你其实在某种程度上已经回答了我的问题，你也回答了最后一个，但为了我个人的理解，我想确认一下——在演讲一开始，你……

cues.en: You spent a lot of time on genetics. You had the fat twins and the fat cow, and the skinny cow, and fat mouse. And you sort of abandoned that toward the end of the talk. So I infer that everybody has their genetic predisposition, which they start with, and their sugar intake regulates them around that? Or what does that describe? The question is, what role does genetics play when it comes to, like, there's an obesity epidemic. The experts will tell you, obviously, our genes haven't changed.
cues.zh: 你花了很多时间讲基因。你提到了胖双胞胎、胖牛和瘦牛，还有肥胖小鼠。但在演讲快结束时，你好像就不怎么提这点了。所以我是不是可以理解为：每个人一开始都有各自的基因易感性，而摄入的糖分则围绕着这种底色来调节体重？还是说应该怎么解释？问题在于，面对当前的肥胖流行病，基因到底扮演了什么角色？专家们肯定会说，显然我们的基因并没有改变。

cues.en: What I'm arguing is, one of the fundamental observations is that you don't see obesity in any animals in the wild. On the east coast where I used to live, there's a deer epidemic. There's obviously enough food for all the deer to overeat, but you don't get fatter deer. You get more deer. You don't get obese deer. So the question is, why do they get fat? Why do they stay lean, in effect, regardless of how much they eat?
cues.zh: 我想说的是，一个最基本的观察是，你在野生动物中看不到肥胖。在我以前住的东海岸，鹿群泛滥成灾。显然有足够的食物让所有的鹿暴饮暴食，但鹿并没有变胖。而是鹿变多了。你根本见不到肥胖的鹿。所以问题是，为什么它们会长胖？其实不管吃多少，为什么它们都能保持苗条？

cues.en: And actually, it's interesting for hibernatives, for instance. They'll get fat yearly, regardless of how much they eat. So they're fat tissues regulated. And what are the genes responding to with us? And I would say they're responding to basically how we process the carbs in the diet. So if we all grew up in a carb-free environment, if we were Inuits, or Maasai, or native Plains Indians, the Great Plains, and we didn't have the carbs in the diet, we would all be lean.
cues.zh: 实际上，比如冬眠动物就很有意思。不管吃多少，它们每年都会长胖。所以它们的脂肪组织是受调控的。那我们体内的基因又是在对什么起反应呢？我认为，它们基本上是在对我们代谢饮食中碳水化合物的方式起反应。所以，如果我们都在没有碳水的环境中长大，如果我们是因纽特人、马赛人，或者是大平原上的北美原住民，饮食中没有碳水，我们全都会很苗条。

cues.en: And then when you grow up in a high-carb environment, then the phenotype manifests itself of obesity. And what the genes are responding to are the carbs in the diet. It's basically how you metabolize them, how much insulin you secrete, how sensitive your fat tissue is to that insulin, and things like that. And what's interesting, again, is...
cues.zh: 而当你在高碳水环境中长大时，肥胖的表型就会显现出来。基因所反应的，正是饮食中的碳水。基本上就是你如何代谢它们，你分泌了多少胰岛素，你的脂肪组织对这种胰岛素有多敏感，诸如此类。再次值得注意的是……

cues.en: I used to live in New York up until a year ago, and I did my coffee from a bagel shop downstairs. This was right around the corner from NYU. And it was full of these, you know, heavy-set young girls from NYU who were eating their low-fat, their bagels, and their low-fat soy cream cheese, and their low-fat soy lattes. And they were doing exactly what the government thinks they should do, and they've been told to do, to live a healthy lifestyle. And I assumed they believed they were just doomed to be overweight, because they were doing what they were told to do.
cues.zh: 直到一年前我还住在纽约，我常在楼下一家百吉饼店买咖啡。就在 NYU（纽约大学）拐角处。店里到处都是 NYU 那些身材偏胖的年轻女孩，吃着低脂百吉饼、抹着低脂大豆奶油芝士，喝着低脂大豆拿铁。她们完全按照政府倡导的、被告知的方式去过所谓健康的生活。我想她们大概觉得自己注定要超重，因为她们明明照做了却还是这样。

cues.en: And the argument I would make is they're doing it in a high-carb environment. And if they didn't live in a high-carb environment, if they didn't eat the carbs, they would be lean. Their phenotype wouldn't manifest itself. And the message I'm trying, this is sort of the battle that I'm trying to fight is to get these ideas across because there are a lot of people out there like obese children who are being tortured with starvation diets and being made to run five miles a day or whatever. And that's not why they're fat.
cues.zh: 我想说的是，她们身处高碳水环境中。如果她们不生活在高碳水环境中，如果不吃那些碳水，她们就会很苗条。她们的肥胖表型就不会显现出来。我想传达的信息，也是我努力在打的这场仗，就是传播这些观点，因为外面有很多人，比如肥胖儿童，正在饱受节食饥饿的折磨，每天被逼着跑五英里什么的。但那根本不是他们变胖的原因。

cues.en: And the problem is they're tortured like that, and then they get their Gatorade when it's over. And they count the 300 calories of Gatorade, and they go, OK, this is good. I'm in negative energy balance. And they're still driving fat accumulation. So we have to get the carbs out of their life. And I sound like a quack diet book doctor when I say that. That's what the research shows. All right. I have a very practical question. So my question is, how do you actually do it? How do you avoid the carbs? You go into a store. You want to buy bacon. You look in the ingredients. There's sugar in there.
cues.zh: 问题是他们受了这么大罪，结束后却喝了瓶佳得乐。他们算着佳得乐的这 300 卡路里，心里想着：很好，我处于能量负平衡状态。可这依然在促进脂肪囤积。所以我们必须把碳水从他们的生活中剔除。虽然我这么说听起来很像江湖饮食书医生。但研究结果就是如此。好的。我有一个非常实际的问题。我的问题是，你到底该怎么做？怎么去避开碳水？你走进一家店。想买培根。你看一下配料表。里面竟然有糖。

cues.en: You come here in Google cafes, there's sugar everywhere, like every meat dish, every stew, they're going to put sugar in. If you want to buy meat, they're going to give you lean cuts of meat. You can get nice fat cuts of meat. So how do you get fat? Well, you can, but it's difficult. I mean, the idea is you can always eat less of it. So if you get the kids off the sodas and the fruit juices, and you don't try to give them low-fat foods.
cues.zh: 你到Google的咖啡厅来，到处都是糖，每道肉菜、每份炖菜，他们都会加糖。你想买肉，他们给你的都是瘦肉。你也能买到不错的肥肉。那怎么吃到肥肉？可以，但很难。我的意思是，办法就是少吃点。所以，让孩子不喝汽水和果汁，也别给他们吃什么低脂食品。

cues.en: You don't try to give them the low-fat yogurt. I actually have this ongoing argument with my wife where I say, look, this is my Michael Pollan kind of thing. If a food makes a health claim, look to see how much sugar is in it. Because almost invariably, with the exception, I think, of Cheerios, weirdly enough, it's going to have a high sugar content. So the best you can do is eat less.
cues.zh: 别给他们低脂酸奶。我其实一直和妻子争论，我说，你看，这算是我Michael Pollan式的观点。如果一种食品宣称健康，就看看它含多少糖。因为几乎无一例外——我觉得奇怪的是，Cheerios除外——它的含糖量都会很高。所以你能做的最好办法就是少吃。

cues.en: So, you know, again, my kids will eat bacon that's cured, apple cured bacon, which I assume means it's sweet and it tastes sweet and there's sugar in it, but it's still better than Frosted Flakes or, you know, Cocoa Puffs or getting apple juice with their, so you can always improve and everyone, it sounds more difficult than, you made it sound difficult, but the reality is when you, you know, when people try it without looking as closely as you do.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，再说一次，我的孩子会吃腌培根，苹果腌培根，我猜那意味着它偏甜、吃起来甜、里面有糖，但仍比Frosted Flakes、Cocoa Puffs，或者让他们配着苹果汁吃要好。所以总能改进。而且大家——听起来比实际更难，你说得让它听起来很难，但现实是，人们去尝试的时候，并不像你这样看得那么细。

cues.en: They, at least the ones who succeed email me and tell me. I don't know if there's this huge background of people who fail on these diets. I don't think they work for everybody because I think after a point you can get, and this is what the British physician wrote about 50 years ago looking at his 1,500 people he put on a...
cues.zh: 他们，至少成功的人会发邮件告诉我。我不知道是不是有很多人在这类饮食法上失败。我不认为它对所有人都有效，因为我觉得到某个点你会变得——这是那位英国医生约50年前写的，他观察了自己让1500人采用的一种……

cues.en: a low-carb diet, and he said the ones who had been fat for a long time were very obese, who had been obese the longest, and women more so than men, because women have, the sex hormones are much more, play a much greater role in their fattening, and these people, it's sort of, they may reach the point of no return.
cues.zh: 低碳水饮食，他说，那些胖了很久的人已经非常肥胖，尤其是肥胖时间最长的人；女性比男性更明显，因为女性的性激素在发胖中作用大得多。而这些人，某种程度上可能已经到了无法回头的地步。

cues.en: But again, the argument I'm making is that if you look at the heart disease risk factors and other profiles, I recently had to post on my blog my own lipid profile, which I got measured, because people wanted to know if I appeared to be killing myself, and I'm not by standard measures anyway. But if you look at that, it would still be a healthier diet. So you do better. You don't have to avoid sugar entirely. You might be healthier if you do. But we could certainly all cut back on it.
cues.zh: 但再说一次，我的论点是，如果你看心脏病风险因素和其他指标，我最近不得不在博客上贴出自己的血脂谱，我去测了，因为人们想知道我是不是在自杀，而按标准指标看，我反正没有。但如果你看那个，它仍会是一种更健康的饮食。所以你会做得更好。你不必完全避免糖。完全避免可能会更健康。但我们肯定都可以少吃点。

cues.en: OK, so maybe I should give a little bit of clarification. So yes, I mean, if you want to go healthier than the average, you can certainly do what you are saying, and you are going to make lots of progress. I did, me personally, I made lots of progress. But if you want to go to the next step, and if you want to completely cut the sugar out and be really healthy, how do you practically do it? Well, first of all, you stop working in an office. See, I work at home.
cues.zh: 好，也许我该稍微澄清一下。是的，我的意思是，如果你想比普通人更健康，你当然可以照你说的做，而且会有很大进展。我自己就取得了很大进展。但如果你想再进一步，想彻底戒掉糖、真正健康，实际该怎么做？首先，别在办公室上班。瞧，我在家工作。

cues.en: So I can control it. I live in Berkeley. I'm sure you have it here. So we have these gourmet butchers from farms that raise their animals humanely and don't put sugar in things. Again, I'm just a journalist. I can't solve every problem. I'm trying to fight this particular battle. And then I hope that if I make some progress and the other people out there fighting this battle make some progress and maybe the whole society will move into a point where it will get easier.
cues.zh: 所以我能控制。我住在伯克利，我相信你们这儿也有。我们有那种高品质肉铺，肉源自人道放养且不加糖的农场。话说回来，我只是个记者，不可能解决所有问题。我只是想打好眼下这一仗。我希望如果我能取得一些进展，其他同样在为此努力的人也能有所突破，那么整个社会或许就会朝着让这件事变得更容易的方向发展。

cues.en: I have a lot of fans at Microsoft, I hate to say, and they've been trying to get the Microsoft, you know, wellness group to put sort of low-carb lines in their cafes, so they have at least, you know, the effect of Atkins-like choices. And so far, as far as I know, they've had no luck, but, you know, given time. Okay, thank you. Hi. I was wondering, you mentioned, like, five studies that were unpublished.
cues.zh: 说来惭愧，我在 Microsoft 有不少粉丝，他们一直试图让 Microsoft 的健康管理部门在员工餐厅引入低碳水专线，这样大家至少能有类似阿特金斯饮食的选择。据我所知，到目前为止他们还没成功，但假以时日或许可以。好的，谢谢。嗨，我想问一下，你之前提到了大概五项未发表的研究。

cues.en: And how many of them are now published, or do you think there's a publication bias where these kind of studies that don't fit the dogma don't ever get published? Actually, they virtually have all been published that I know of. Probably several dozen studies published. I mean, the results are always the same. People on these diets, they lose more weight, their triglycerides go down more, their HDL goes up more.
cues.zh: 其中有多少现在已经发表了？还是说你觉得存在发表偏见，导致这类不符合主流教条的研究根本无法发表？其实就我所知，它们几乎都发表了。大概发表了几十项研究吧。我是说，结果总是一样的：采用这种饮食的人减重更多，甘油三酯降得更多，高密度脂蛋白升得更多。

cues.en: you know, everything gets better. It's basically the metabolic syndrome insulin resistance resolves. It goes away and should go away if I'm right, because it's pretty obviously caused by the carbs in the diet. There are publication biases. For instance, people who go in believing that it's all about calories will interpret their data to make it all about calories, even if they publish that the, you know, Atkins group does better than the American Heart Association group.
cues.zh: 你看，各项指标都变好了。基本上代谢综合征和胰岛素抵抗都缓解了。它们消失了，如果我是对的，那它们本来就该消失，因为这显然是饮食中的碳水化合物引起的。发表偏见确实存在。比如那些坚信“一切全看热量”的人，即便发表的数据显示阿特金斯组比美国心脏协会推荐组表现更好，他们也会把数据硬解释成热量的作用。

cues.en: There are people who all, there are now like low-carb journals out there, the Journal of Nutrition and Metabolism. So some people will do, there's a great study done on type 2 diabetes at Duke University where most of the subjects were able to get off their diabetes medications. It was supposedly an irreversible disease. And the author, the first author, only sent it to the Journal of Nutrition and Metabolism where it would basically be read by the converted because he didn't want to deal with
cues.zh: 现在甚至有了专门的低碳水期刊，比如《Journal of Nutrition and Metabolism》。所以有些人会——杜克大学曾做过一项针对 2 型糖尿病的出色研究，大多数受试者都成功停掉了降糖药。而这本被认为是一种不可逆的疾病。但第一作者只把它投给了《Journal of Nutrition and Metabolism》，基本上只有同道中人会看，因为他不想去应付

cues.en: all the flack he would get trying to publish in the mainline journal. So there are definitely biases. But if you do these studies now, I think you almost have you, there's a clinical trials website where you have to register them. And part of the reason for that is to make sure that people don't only publish positive results. So they pretty much all get published, but they do get spun. And often the spin takes over, you know, one.
cues.zh: 试图在主流期刊上发表时会招致的猛烈抨击。所以偏见绝对是存在的。但现在做这类研究，大家几乎都必须在临床试验网站上注册。这样做的部分原因，就是为了防止人们只发表正面结果。所以它们基本都能发表，但会被粉饰曲解。而这种曲解往往会占据上风。

cues.en: The biggest study ever done came out of it was Pennsylvania, UPenn, Colorado, and University of Cincinnati. And they put 300 subjects on an Atkins diet and effect and an American Heart Association diet. And they referred to it as a low carb versus a low fat diet. This is a classic way to do it. But the low fat diet is calorie restricted.
cues.zh: 史上规模最大的研究出自 Pennsylvania、UPenn、Colorado 和 University of Cincinnati。他们让 300 名受试者分别采用 Atkins diet 和美国心脏协会饮食。他们称之为低碳水 vs 低脂饮食。这是经典做法。但低脂饮食是限制热量的。

cues.en: So when you're told to go on the low-fat diet, you're told to eat, you know, 14, 1500 calories a day, basically semi-starve yourself. And when you go on the low-carb diet, you're told to eat as much as you want. Just don't eat carbohydrates. And, you know, one of the lessons I learned writing about physics is it's absolutely crucial to define your terms carefully so people know what they've done, what you've done and can replicate it. And so you're not, in effect, trying to fool people.
cues.zh: 所以让你采用低脂饮食时，会告诉你每天吃 1400、1500 卡路里，基本上就是半饥饿。而采用低碳水饮食时，会告诉你想吃多少吃多少，只要别吃碳水化合物。你知道，我写物理时学到的教训之一是：必须仔细定义术语，这绝对关键，这样人们才知道他们做了什么、你做了什么，并能复现。这样你实际上就不是在试图糊弄人。

cues.en: And if I was writing that study, you would say low-fat, low-calorie versus low-carb ad libitum. Ad libitum means eat as much as you want. And I would always use those terms. Because you never want to forget that one group is low-calorie and one group is ad libitum. Because that also suggests, in this case, they got essentially the same weight loss. The Atkins group did better on heart disease risk factors, but the weight loss was virtually the same. And you want people to remember...
cues.zh: 如果我来写那项研究，我会说低脂、低热量 vs 低碳水 ad libitum。Ad libitum 意思是想吃多少吃多少。我会一直用这些说法。因为你绝不能忘记一组是低热量，另一组是 ad libitum。因为这也说明，在这个案例里，他们减重基本相同。Atkins 组在心脏病风险因素上表现更好，但减重几乎一样。而你想让人们记住……

cues.en: that one group is being semi-starved and one group isn't, because that's evidence that it's not about the calories. And they just didn't do it. They mentioned it in their methodology that the low-fat group was calorie restricted, and then they ignored it. And the title was low-fat versus low-carb. And the papers picked it up, low-fat versus low-carb. And they left out the crucial ingredient, which is one diet restricts calories and the other diet doesn't, which is the ingredient that tells you your paradigm might be wrong.
cues.zh: 一组处于半饥饿状态，另一组没有，因为这是证据，说明问题不在热量。而他们就是没这么做。他们在方法部分提到低脂组限制了热量，然后就忽略了。标题是低脂 vs 低碳水。论文也照搬成低脂 vs 低碳水。他们漏掉了关键因素：一种饮食限制热量，另一种不限制；而这个因素告诉你，你的范式可能错了。

cues.en: I'm just wondering if any of your research came across any connections between people who drop the carbohydrates, but coincidentally, they're also dropping the trans fats, because most of the carbohydrates we've purchased commercially are public with trans fats, which tend to be the worst fats for you in terms of heart disease risk. You know, it's funny, because I would always argue it the other way. To me, the evidence of trans fats are bad.
cues.zh: 我只是想知道，你的研究有没有发现这种关联：人们戒掉碳水化合物，但碰巧也戒掉了反式脂肪，因为我们商业化购买的大多数碳水化合物都含有反式脂肪，而反式脂肪在心脏病风险方面往往是对你最不利的脂肪。你知道，这很有趣，因为我总是反过来论证。在我看来，反式脂肪有害的证据……

cues.en: Comes from mostly from observational studies where you compare people eat a lot of trans fats to people eat very little like the nurses health studies what they're doing is they're when you think who eats a lot of trans fats and who doesn't You're comparing in effect people buy a lot of processed foods and fast foods to people who cook most of their meals for themselves
cues.zh: 主要来自观察性研究：比较吃很多反式脂肪的人和吃得很少的人，比如 Nurses' Health Studies。他们所做的其实是——你想想谁吃很多反式脂肪、谁不吃，你实际上是在比较买很多加工食品和快餐的人，和大部分饭菜都自己做的人。

cues.en: You can but you're also but the point is that as you put it the processed foods come with the carbs I don't the trans fat data just doesn't wow me I mean it is true if you give up the carbs you're gonna have to give up the trans fats But remember all those populations I talked about in the beginning like the Trinidadians the Sioux Native Americans Soo, they would not have been getting trans fats. So we don't know what their heart disease risk was
cues.zh: 你可以这么说，但重点是，正如你所说，加工食品会带着碳水一起来。我……反式脂肪的数据就是说服不了我。我的意思是，确实，如果你戒掉碳水，你就得戒掉反式脂肪。但记住我一开始谈到的那些人群，比如特立尼达人、苏族原住民。所以，他们不会摄入反式脂肪。我们也就不知道他们的心脏病风险是多少。

cues.en: But we know that they weren't getting margarine. There wasn't a food industry forcing trans fats on them. So it's quite likely the obvious, again, the null hypothesis would be the carb content of the diet. And then my second question is that there are populations that tend not to eat meat like India. There are so many vegetarians. They get their proteins mainly from legumes. So what is your take on the glycemic index of legumes and other non-meat sources of proteins for people who aren't really eating meat?
cues.zh: 但我们知道，他们并没有吃人造黄油。没有食品行业把反式脂肪强加给他们。所以很可能，显然，再次说，零假设应该是饮食中的碳水含量。然后我的第二个问题是，有些人群往往不吃肉，比如印度。那里有很多素食者。他们主要从豆类获取蛋白质。那么，对于并不真正吃肉的人，你怎么看豆类和其他非肉类蛋白质来源的升糖指数？

cues.en: Well, I do think, again, the argument I make in the book, like the book is called Why We Get Fat, not how to lose weight. And the reason I call it Why We Get Fat is I want to make this argument that it's literally about the carbs, high glycemic index carbs, which doesn't, you know, the legumes are lower glycemic index, green vegetables are low glycemic index, and the sugars. And anyone can improve their diet.
cues.zh: 我认为，还是回到我在书里的观点，比如这本书叫《我们为什么会发胖》，而不是《如何减肥》。之所以起这个名字，是因为我想说明问题完全出在碳水上，也就是高升糖指数的碳水——豆类的升糖指数较低，绿叶蔬菜也低——还有糖。任何人都可以改善饮食，

cues.en: if they just remove the sugars and the white flour, and to some extent, what we call whole wheat flour in the United States. And actually, even in one of the observations that I wrote about good calories, bad calories, as early as 1907, the British Medical Association had a meeting in which they had a discussion about the diabetes problem in India, because diabetes was rampant. And they said it's actually worse among the vegetarian sex.
cues.zh: 只要戒掉糖和白面粉，在某种程度上还包括我们在美国所说的全麦面粉。实际上，我在《好卡路里，坏卡路里》中记录的一个观察就提到，早在1907年，英国医学会就开会讨论过印度的糖尿病问题，因为当时那里的糖尿病十分猖獗。他们表示，这种情况在素食群体中其实更为严重，

cues.en: probably because they were also eating the most sugar, which they suggested in 1907. But you can improve the diet by removing the fat and carbohydrates, regardless, is the point. But if someone is very predisposed to get fat, if someone's 300 pounds, I would argue that you have to get, basically, they're not going to get enough calories. The easiest way to maximize calories and minimize carbs is with animal products.
cues.zh: 很可能是因为他们吃的糖也最多，这是他们在1907年提出的观点。但核心在于，无论如何，你都可以通过戒掉精制碳水来改善饮食。可如果某人极易发胖，比如体重有300磅，我认为他们基本上就很难摄入足够的热量。而在把碳水降到最低的同时保证热量，最简单的办法就是吃动物类食品。

cues.en: And so that's the problem. So if these people, you know, they could improve on a vegetarian diet, and I get emails all the day from people telling me how much they lost just giving up sugars, I don't think that's enough. In my experience, I could just ask myself, like, what would happen if I added whole-wheat pasta back to my diet, say, three times a week? And I'm, you know, I could pretty much bet that I'd gain 10 pounds. But...
cues.zh: 所以问题就在这里。虽然这些人靠素食也能改善健康，我也天天收到邮件说自己光是戒糖就瘦了多少，但我认为这还不够。以我的经验，我就问自己，如果我重新把全麦意面加入饮食，比如一周吃三次，会怎么样？我几乎敢打赌自己会胖上10磅。但是……

cues.en: You know, the point is anyone can lose weight just by getting rid of it and improve their risk profiles because the argument I make is these high glycemic index carbs and sugars are the cause of the chronic diseases that associate with obesity and diabetes and insulin resistance. And then, you know, if it's an all-vegetarian or vegan diet, you're still going to be better. You may not be as lean as you could be if you threw your ethical considerations to the wind and switched to meat, but you will be healthier than if you keep these foods in your diet.
cues.zh: 关键在于，任何人只要戒掉这些就能变瘦，并改善健康风险指标，因为我的观点是，高升糖指数碳水和糖正是肥胖、糖尿病和胰岛素抵抗等慢性病的根源。而且，哪怕是纯素饮食，你的状况依然会变好。虽然可能不如抛开伦理考量改吃肉那样精瘦，但绝对比继续吃这些高碳水食物要健康得多。

cues.en: I was wondering about people who do a lot of athletics, especially endurance stuff, and talk about things like carb loading and other studies that have recently suggested that women specifically recover better when they eat carbs after a meal, too, and how that moves in all of this. The question is about how, what about athletics and endurance exercise? Don't you need the carbohydrates? Aren't it crucial?
cues.zh: 我一直在想那些经常运动、特别是练耐力项目的人，大家常说“碳水补给”，最近也有其他研究表明女性在餐后补充碳水恢复得更好，这些又该怎么解释呢？所以问题是，经常运动和做耐力训练的人该怎么办？难道不需要碳水吗？它难道不是必需的吗？

cues.en: This is not my area of expertise. And I was not an endurance athlete. But in the late 1970s, early 1980s, there was some research done at the University of Vermont by a fellow named Steve Finney, who's now an emeritus professor of nutrition at UC Davis. And he put professional bike racers on ketogenic diets. And it takes about three weeks to what's called keto adopt, where you adopt completely to the complete lack of carbs in the diet and the fat.
